## D-229 - Missing-data entries carry an optional typed cause beside their sentence; nothing reads it yet (2026-11-12)

Principles P10 (an unknown cause stays unknown), P11 (decide by codes, not
wording), P20 and P21. Round 2, step S4.5a. D-218 put typed codes beside
field-conflict sentences and D-219 to D-226 moved those readers to them; the
gap and provider-status readers (inventory groups G and P) were left because a
code on a `ManifestEntry` is stored with Stage B output and reports. The
owner's ruling for this step: "New reports may store codes, missing-data
entries may carry codes ... Additions to stored data only." This step only
writes; no reader decides by a code yet.

Choice: optional `ManifestEntry.cause`, listed once in `GAP_CAUSES`
(`src/types/refusalCause.ts`, beside the conflict list; no name is shared).
The writer that composes the sentence writes the code beside it, unchanged;
a code is never derived from a sentence, never filled in on an older entry,
and an entry without one is unresolved. `ManifestEntrySchema` accepts the
listed codes only, so an unknown value is refused, never mapped to a member.

Producer sites and their codes:

- `valueCompanyCore` (`stageB/valuation.ts`), the unprofitable-overlay DCF
  suppression on `valuation.dcf`: `dcf-unprofitable-overlay` (G1, G2).
- `buildDcfAssumptions`, on `valuation.dcf.salesToCapital`: missing balance
  fields `invested-capital-balance-fields-missing` (G4); a refused
  temporary-equity claim `invested-capital-temporary-equity-refused` and
  lease-emptied capital `invested-capital-lease-emptied` (G3).
- `supplementTemporaryEquity` (`edgar/temporaryEquityEnrichment.ts`): a
  withheld balance date `temporary-equity-enrichment-withheld`, an unmatched
  category `temporary-equity-operands-unmatched` (G5).
- The FMP client: `FmpQuotaError` `fmp-quota` (P1; the retry note appended
  later keeps it, the sentence still states the rate limit); a 200 with an
  empty array, live and fixture paths, `fmp-empty-array` (P2, P3, P5);
  "no API key + no fixture" `fmp-no-api-key` (P5); a symbol-scope
  `FmpAccessError` `fmp-symbol-restricted` (P7a). An endpoint-scope
  refusal, an object body, HTTP and schema errors carry none.
- The EDGAR ticker lookup: `ticker "<symbol>" not in SEC company_tickers.json`
  `sec-ticker-not-listed` (P5).
- `selectAnnualFiling` (`dataBundle.ts`), a successor registrant's
  no-annual-report gap: `sec-unlinked-predecessor` (P4), and the item 1A,
  MD&A, business and 10-K notes gaps that quote that gap whole, since
  `withResolvedPredecessor` reads all five.

Three rewrites turn a gap into a sentence that no longer states its cause, so
they drop the code (`withoutGapCause`, `stageA/manifest.ts`): the FIN-OTHER
"Prior DCF suppression retained" sentence (`compute.ts`), the expected
segmentation gap (`markSegmentationGapExpected`) and a resolved predecessor
(`withResolvedPredecessor`). Not coded: P6 and P7b (their readers match
sentences no single writer composes), S1 (non-bank lenders, owner decision),
the C sites (conflicts, D-218), G6 and the identity comparisons (they need a
link between refusals), G7 and O1 (already typed, D-223) and the R group
(saved reports, P21).

Where the code is removed, and why. It is stored data for the pipeline's own
readers, so it never reaches a model or a reader: the Stage C payload
(`assembleContextPayload` returns the payload without any entry's code: the
model receives nothing new; the frozen Stage C payload record and every
same-report `payload.txt` are byte-identical); run-input snapshots
(`captureRunInputSnapshot`, as D-218 did for conflict codes until read, so a
snapshot of the same inputs has the same bytes); the full-report request
schema (`removePipelineOwnedRequestFields`); the dossier's
`data-report-identity` hash; and the report-summary API
(`/api/report/view/[reportId]`, whose client check refuses unknown entry
keys). The judge, analyst and full-report request schemas have the SHA-256
they have on main (f66130f4..., 27e0dcd9..., 1e1e8574...). The surface
manifest declares `cause` the one stored-only `ManifestEntry` field
(`MANIFEST_ENTRY_STORED_ONLY_KEYS`); its test still checks the full field set.

Agreement. For each consumer, its wording test was compared with the code
test that keeps the consumer's other conditions (`tests/helpers/
gapCauseAgreement.ts`). Over every entry the producers write in
`tests/gapCause.dualWrite.test.ts` (each site with a positive case and
controls) and over the DEMO audit fixture rebuilt from current code, they
agree on every site. Over the 17 same-report cases (5,490 entries in Stage B
output and reports) no entry carries a code its wording contradicts: G1 and
G2 agree on RIVN; every other wording match (76 P7a, 76 G5, 2 P2 entries) is
an entry restored from a run-input snapshot taken before D-229, which has no
code and is unresolved, as intended. One disagreement is pinned in the test,
not hidden: when the keyless fallback fails after FMP returned an empty
profile, it appends its failure to FMP's sentence, which still states the
empty array and keeps `fmp-empty-array`; the job runner's and company page's
`reason === FMP_EMPTY_ARRAY_REASON` no longer matches it (and so, today, does
not call the ticker unknown although EDGAR confirmed the issuer). The step
that moves P2/P5 to the code must keep that outcome.

Frozen record. The DEMO audit-fixture record (`tests/fixtures/frozen/
audit-fixture-current.json`) gains exactly 22 leaves, all `fmp-no-api-key`:
`stageB.gaps[0..10].cause` and `report.appendix.missingData[0..10].cause`;
the record's own digest of the projection (`projectionSha256`) changes with
them. It was re-recorded with `npm run freeze:refresh -- --target
audit-fixture --decision D-229` scoped to exactly those 23 paths (record
SHA-256 2face745... to 47950c52...); the log entry is in
`tests/fixtures/frozen/refresh-log.json`, and with `cause` and the digest
removed the record is identical to before. The Stage C payload record is
unchanged.

Same-report check (17 cases, 136 files, against main at e5f0a3d6): two files
differ, both RIVN and both only by added `cause` leaves:
`rivn-data-only/stageB.json` (`gaps.113.cause`, `valuation.gaps.14.cause`) and
`rivn-data-only/report.json` (`appendix.missingData.114.cause`), each
`dcf-unprofitable-overlay`. Every `payload.txt`, `report.md`, `print.html`,
`audit.md`, `web-classic.html` and `web-dossier.html` is byte-identical.

P21: saved reports are untouched and not migrated; a saved report without
codes parses as before. No version stamp moves (report spec 1.73.0, payload
1.92.0, Stage B implementation version): nothing a reader sees or a model
receives changes.

Later steps: move each G and P consumer to its code, with the entry's legacy
wording read in one place for entries without a code (as
`src/edgar/refusalCauseRead.ts` does for conflicts), and lower its count in
`tests/refusalWording.ratchet.test.ts`; stop removing a code from snapshots
once a reader reads it; G2 reads the result's `suppressionReason`, so moving it
needs the code on the valuation result as well. Out of scope here: switching
any consumer, links between copied refusals, saved-report readers, S1.

## D-228 - Only METIS_ names configure Metis; a leftover THESIS_ name stops startup (2026-11-12)

Principles P23, P24 and P26. Revises D-21 (the `X-Thesis-Token` header and the
`THESIS_RESUME_ON_START` name) and D-143 / B11-OD-5 (the startup warning about
conflicting aliases and canonical-over-alias precedence), and the rebrand's
compatibility promise in docs/BRAND.md that `THESIS_*` names stay accepted.

**Problem.** Since the rebrand every `METIS_*` setting also answered to a
`THESIS_*` alias (`metisEnv`, `withMetisAliases` in `src/config/namespace.ts`).
The owner's `.env` and launcher have now been renamed, with a proof that every
setting reads the same value before and after. Removing the aliases quietly
would be unsafe for anyone still on an old file: a leftover
`THESIS_RESUME_ON_START=0` would be ignored and queued paid work would resume
at startup, a `THESIS_MAX_JOB_COST_USD` cap would vanish, and a
`THESIS_DB_PATH` would move the app to a different database.

**Options.** (a) Keep the aliases. (b) Remove them and ignore old names.
(c) Remove them and refuse old names explicitly.

**Choice: (c).** Only `METIS_*` names configure Metis. Each of the 19 names
that used to be an alias (`RETIRED_ALIAS_SUFFIXES`: the 15 `METIS_*` schema
keys plus `ALLOWED_HOST`, `DB_PATH`, `DATA_DIR` and `IMPORT_LEGACY_DB`) is
refused when its `THESIS_` form is present, set to anything including blank.
The refusal is one `StaleSettingsError` that lists every stale name with its
`METIS_` replacement and never a value. Names are looked up directly, so a
native Windows environment matches case-insensitively exactly where the old
alias read did, and ordinary records keep exact case.

**Where the refusal runs.** It lives in one owner, `src/config/namespace.ts`.
`metisEnv` and `projectMetisSettings` are the only readers of a formerly
aliased setting, and both refuse before they read; a source-scan test
(`tests/config.retiredSettings.test.ts`) fails if src reads a `METIS_*` or
`THESIS_*` environment name any other way (only `METIS_RUNTIME_BUILD_ID`,
which never had an alias, is read directly). So `getConfig`/`parseEnv`, the
database and data paths, the legacy-import switch, the allowed host and the
judge-order fallback all refuse on first use, in the server, the request
proxy, the job runner and scheduler bootstrap, and every script that reads a
setting. The server also refuses eagerly in `src/instrumentation.ts` before it
mints the request token or starts the scheduler, prints the message and
exits with code 1. (Next.js only logs a `register()` failure and keeps
listening; checked on the production build, every page and API route then
answered a bare 500, no token file or database was created and the scheduler
never ran. Exiting makes the refusal plain.) The settings:reset,
costs:reconcile, research:replay and export:corrected entry points refuse
eagerly as well, because replay of a `--snapshot` file and the corrected
export read no setting. The golden harness reads its database path through
`metisEnv`; its workers get a stripped environment and run unchanged.

**Request header.** `X-Metis-Token` behaves exactly as before. A request that
carries only `X-Thesis-Token` is refused with the same 403 as any other token
failure and the reason "the X-Thesis-Token header is no longer accepted; send
the same token in the X-Metis-Token header instead". The old header is never
read as a credential, including by the company-page proxy check. Every client
in the repository sends `X-Metis-Token`.

**Kept.** Every setting's meaning, validation and default (spend caps, resume
hold, statement source, rolling window, concurrency, token path, lease timings,
stream idle, reservation mode, judge order, EV leases, allowed host, UI flag);
legacy data-folder and file discovery (`Thesis`, `thesis.db`, `Thesis/ai`);
`METIS_IMPORT_LEGACY_DB` and its warning; old-database upgrades; the Claude API
integration. A table of 157 METIS_-only inputs (blank, padded, valid, boundary
and invalid values for every setting, plus lease combinations) parses to
exactly the same result as main at e55519ce, frozen in
`tests/fixtures/config-parity-before-d228.json`.

**Frozen wording.** Ten strings that reach saved reports, exports or the
judge prompt still spell `THESIS_STATEMENT_SOURCE`, `THESIS_EV_INCLUDE_LEASES`
and `THESIS_JUDGE_ORDER` (`src/pipeline/keyless.ts`, `stageB/valuation.ts`,
`stageB/returns.ts`, `stageC/judgeProtocol.ts`'s `JUDGE_ORDER_ENV_KEY`). They
are unchanged byte for byte here, because rewording them changes report text
and prompt bytes and needs an owner decision; the source-scan test pins each
line. Comments, Settings text, logs and docs use the `METIS_*` names.

**Risks and reversibility.** Anyone with an old `.env`, launcher or shell
variable must rename keys before the next start; the error says which and how.
Reverting this change restores the aliases. No stored report, ledger row or
data file changes.

## D-227 - New reports record which exact build assembled them; nothing reads it yet (2026-11-12)

Principles P27 and P20. A saved report names its rules only through
hand-kept stamps (`meta.specVersion`, `meta.pipelineVersion`,
`meta.evidenceContract`), and many commits share the same stamps, so a report
could not say which code made it. The built app already proves its own
identity: `scripts/build-with-identity.mjs` writes
`.next/runtime-artifact-identity.json`, and run-input snapshot custody records
it. The architecture review proposed replacing the stamps with that identity
(Proposal 1); its critique revised that: add the identity without deleting any
format, method or display contract until each consumer is inventoried; an
identity locates code, it does not retain or execute it; a report made by
different code is not a report whose figures are stale; and a documentation
or renderer change must not demand a paid rerun. The owner chose the
critique's form, never forcing a rerun.

Options: replace the stamps now (rejected by the critique); derive an
identity from the checkout at run time (a dev server's working tree is not the
code that ran, so that would be a guess, P10); or record the verified build
identity as an optional added field. Choice: optional `meta.codeIdentity`,
owned by `src/report/codeIdentity.ts`:

- `codeCommit` (40-64 hex, or null when the build had no project git
  metadata), `dirtyDiffHash` (SHA-256 of the build-time diff of the built
  sources, or null), `methodDocumentHash` (SHA-256 of docs/METHODOLOGY.md as
  the build captured it), `compiledArtifactHash` (SHA-256 of the verified,
  sorted list of compiled module paths relative to the build directory and
  their SHA-256 hashes), `methodArtifactHash` (the combined hash snapshot
  custody already records, so a report can be matched to its snapshot), and
  `dependencyLockHash` (SHA-256 of package-lock.json as the build captured
  it). No machine path, timestamp or build id is stored.
- It comes from `readRuntimeCodeIdentity`
  (`scripts/runtime-artifact-manifest.mjs`), which runs the same checks as the
  snapshot custody reader (build token, manifest format, hash shapes and a
  fresh enumeration of the compiled bytes); that reader's own output is
  unchanged. The job runner is the only writer: after the passes, it records
  the identity on the assembled report and on a data-only report. When no
  verified identity exists (dev server, tests, the same-report harness, the
  CLI, or build evidence that no longer matches) the field is omitted, never
  guessed or filled with placeholders. Linking a recovered verify artifact
  keeps that artifact's own record, as D-217 does for its stamp.
- Saved reports are not migrated (P21). The report schema, and so both read
  modes of the stored-report reader, accept a report with or without it; the
  identity object itself is strict, and unknown fields elsewhere are still
  refused.

Nothing reads it yet: no staleness state, notice, banner, rerun prompt, cache
or resume key, or replay decision. A different identity never forces a rerun.
No surface shows it: the app (both layouts), Markdown, print and audit export
render byte for byte the same with and without it; the dossier's
`data-report-identity` hash leaves it out. It never reaches a model: it is
written after the last pass, no request schema holds report metadata, and it
is on the pipeline-owned removal list, so the judge, analyst and full-report
request schemas are byte-identical to before (SHA-256 compared against main).
`tests/report.codeIdentity.test.ts` fails if any other src file reads it.

The report spec stays 1.73.0 and no stamp moves: as with D-217's
`meta.evidenceContract` and `presumedCostUsd`, this adds one optional meta
field and changes no figure. Out of scope: removing or changing any stamp,
pin, cutoff or contract; any reader of the field. Evidence: `golden:diff`
reports no changes (17 cases, 136 files); the harness has no built identity,
so the field is omitted there.

## D-226 - Refusal codes: the "Revenue scope unresolved" copy keeps only its own code (2026-11-12)

Principle P11. Revises D-222, which left this copy as it was. When
`admitRevenue` (`src/edgar/revenueAdmission.ts`) selects no revenue line and
the filing shows only a contract-revenue note, it keeps the row's refused
revenue conflict and replaces its sentence with "Revenue scope unresolved: the
contract-revenue fact is not established as consolidated operating revenue; a
complete same-period operating line is required." It kept every other
property of the old refusal, including its `cause`, so a code from another
sentence could sit beside the new one, which D-222 rules out.

Which codes reach the line. The line runs only on a refused conflict that
`reconsiderable` accepts: code `revenue-scope`, SEC evidence, or a vendor or
SEC value that agrees with a filed line. Only `admitRevenue` writes a code on
revenue, always `revenue-scope` (the sales-basis refusal, the
conflicting-observations refusal, and this line). Income classification runs
again on the built statements (`src/pipeline/incomeBasis.ts`), so its own
`revenue-scope` refusals do reach the line. The other revenue refusals (the
keyless contract-revenue and filed-operand refusals in
`src/pipeline/keyless.ts`, and income classification's own `refuse`) carry
no code. No writer puts any other code on revenue.

Who reads the result. Two readers decide by the code, both in this file: the
primary-statement override (line 196) and `reconsiderable` (line 68), each
also accepting SEC evidence. The other readers of the revenue conflict
(`incomeClassification.ts`, `incomeBasis.ts`, `compute.ts`, `forensics.ts`)
read `usable`, `resolution`, the values and the evidence, and income
classification copies the sentence into its own uncoded refusal; none reads
the code. The code is kept in run input snapshots (it is not a D-218
dual-written code).

Options considered. (a) Drop the code, as D-222 did for the repurchase copy:
a sales-basis refusal has no SEC evidence and no agreeing value, so without
its code the next pass no longer reconsiders it, and both the decision and the
snapshot bytes change. Rejected. (b) Always write `revenue-scope`: right in
meaning (the sentence states an unresolved revenue scope), but a keyless
refusal without a code would gain one, which changes what new run input
snapshots store and, for a refusal with no SEC evidence, what the two readers
decide. Not decision-neutral, so not done here; it is an accuracy item for
later. (c) Keep `revenue-scope`, the code this writer establishes, and drop any
other code. Choice: (c). A refusal without a code still gets none, because a
code is never added by copying.

Not changed: every decision, sentence and stored byte. For each refusal that
can reach the line the result is the same object, in the same key order, as
before; only a hypothetical conflict carrying another code (none is written
today) now loses that code. `tests/revenueAdmission.scopeUnresolvedCode.test.ts`
builds the refusals with the real writer (`admitRevenue`'s sales-basis and
conflicting-observations refusals, and the keyless sentence from
`contractRevenueScopeRefusal` in the shape the keyless pass stores), reaches
the line, and requires the old form byte for byte, plus an unchanged third
pass. It also shows that dropping the code would change the next pass, and
that another writer's code is dropped. The comparison check (`golden:diff`)
shows no difference.

## D-225 - The "built under older rules" note appears in the audit export (2026-11-12)

Principles P22 and P20. D-217 gave a saved report with no evidence-rules stamp
one reader note, "Built under older rules: this report has no evidence-rules
stamp, so its figures are shown as saved.", and one whose stamp this app does
not know a "Built under unrecognised rules: ..." note. The app's header
notices, the Markdown export and the print export showed it; the audit export
did not, so the same report disclosed its rules on three surfaces and stayed
silent on the fourth. Options considered: leave the audit export silent (two
presentation rules for one fact), write the sentence into the audit export
(a second hand-kept copy), or have the audit export read the one shared rule.
Choice: the last.

The audit export (`src/report/export/auditMarkdown.ts`) now reads
`evidenceContractNotice` (`src/report/presentation.ts`, the one rule from
D-217) and, when it returns a note, shows it in its header block after the
synthetic and provider-fallback notices, as a blockquote with the same
escaping those notices use. That mirrors the Markdown export's header. The
sentence and its condition are unchanged and still live only in
`evidenceContractNotice`.

The approved visible difference is only this: the audit export of a saved
report with no stamp, or with a stamp this app does not recognise, now shows
that one note as the last notice of its header block, before the run section.
A report with the current stamp exports exactly as before. No saved report is
modified (P21), no stamp or version changes, and no other notice, heading,
number or sentence changes. `tests/report.evidenceContract.test.ts` now checks
the audit export on every case it already covered: the note appears once, last
in the header block and after the synthetic or provider-fallback notice; a
stamped report shows none, and its audit export equals the unstamped one with
only the note line removed; the unrecognised-rules note appears once; and the
app, Markdown, print and audit export carry the same sentence for the same
report. One existing snapshot (`tests/stageC.multiClaimReasoning.test.ts`,
the catalyst/risk export goldens of an unstamped legacy fixture) changes only
its audit hash: with the note line removed, the new audit output hashes to the
earlier value. The comparison check (`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80 files) shows
no difference; all its cases are rebuilt with the current stamp.

## D-224 - The "projections not recorded" note appears in the Markdown, print and audit exports (2026-11-12)

Principles P22 and P20. #125 gave the app's classic layout the dossier's note
for a saved report that recorded no projections: a "Weighted Projections"
section reading "Projections were not recorded in this snapshot. No forecast
series or scenario weights are inferred." The Markdown, print and audit
exports rendered nothing for such a report, so the same report said different
things on different surfaces, and the exports left the absence undisclosed.
Options considered: leave the exports silent (keeps two presentation rules for
one fact), copy the sentence into each export (four hand-kept copies), or one
rule in the presentation layer that every surface reads. Choice: the last.

`projectionsNotRecordedNotice` (`src/report/presentation.ts`) holds the
sentence and its condition: the report has no `projections` and the reader
convention `unavailableCashFlowModel` does not hide the section; otherwise it
returns null. That is exactly the app's condition since #125. `ReportView.tsx`
now reads its sentence there (rendered output unchanged), and each export
renders it in the section's normal position in its own style:

- Markdown: `## 12. Weighted Projections`, then `_<sentence>_`, between Future
  Outlook and Macro Context.
- Print: the numbered `report-projections` section heading, then the sentence
  as `<p class="faint">`, between Future Outlook and Macro Context.
- Audit: the export's own projection heading, `## Projection audit trail`, then
  the sentence as a plain paragraph, before the missing-data manifest.

The approved visible difference is only this: a saved report without
projections, whose cash-flow model is not hidden by its reader convention, now
shows that heading and sentence in the three exports. A report with
projections exports exactly as before (the audit export still renders recorded
projections without the reader-convention check), and a report whose
cash-flow model is unavailable gains nothing. No saved report is modified
(P21), no version stamp changes (this is a read-time presentation of older
reports), and no other heading, note, number or sentence changes. None of the
exports has a table of contents that lists the projections section, so none
needed updating. `tests/report.projectionsNotRecordedExports.test.ts` checks
each export's heading, sentence and position, the with-projections and
hidden-model cases, the same sentence on all four surfaces, and that the
sentence is written in only one `src` file. One existing print test
(`tests/report.export.printHtml.test.ts`, "gracefully omits ...") asserted that
a report without projections printed no "Weighted Projections" heading; it now
asserts the heading appears once with the note and no projection content. The
comparison check (`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80 files) shows no difference; all
its cases record projections.

## D-223 - Refusal codes, step 6: the duplicate-period note and the estimate-anchor suffix read a typed value (2026-11-12)

Principle P11. Step 6 of the D-218 migration moves the two remaining general
readers whose sentence is written in memory in the same call, so a typed value
can travel beside it without storing anything new: the statement block's
duplicate-period note (G7, `oneRowPerPeriod`, `src/pipeline/stageC/payload.ts`)
and the estimate-anchor stop suffix (O1, `buildRevenueAnchor`,
`src/pipeline/stageB/valuation.ts`). Both typed values are in-memory only: they
are never stored, serialised or shown, and they are not new stored status
words. No sentence, version stamp, snapshot, Stage B output, payload, report or
export changes.

G7. `normalizeQuarterRowsWithKinds` (`src/pipeline/stageB/quarterWindows.ts`)
is the former body of `normalizeQuarterRows`; each of its five rejection sites
now writes its unchanged `{ period, reason }` record and, in a parallel
`rejectionKinds` array, a `QuarterRejectionKind`: `invalid-date`,
`alias-scope-conflict`, `alias-value-restatement`, `duplicate-missing-recency`
or `duplicate-tied-recency`. One local helper pushes both, so the arrays cannot
drift. `oneRowPerPeriod`, its only caller, notes a period served more than once
when `isAmbiguousDuplicateRejection` holds for its kind (the two duplicate
kinds) instead of when the sentence starts `duplicate fiscal period`.
`normalizeQuarterRows` now calls it and returns exactly `{ rows, rejected }`:
the same keys in the same order, the same array and the same record objects
(keys `period`, `reason`) as before. Options considered: a kind field on each
record (every consumer that spreads or stores a record would carry it), an
extra property on `normalizeQuarterRows`' result (compute.ts passes that whole
object on through `normalizeStatementQuarters` to several more functions), or a
separate function only the reader calls. Choice: the last, the least leak risk.

Equivalence. The two duplicate kinds are written by exactly the two sites whose
sentence starts `duplicate fiscal period`; the other three sentences start
`invalid fiscal period-end date` or `fiscal aliases`, and every sentence begins
with fixed text, so no period or provider value can change what it starts
with. The kinds therefore name the same records, in the same order, so the
notes are the same. `tests/stageC.duplicatePeriodKind.test.ts` feeds every
kind (both duplicate kinds, a duplicate across fiscal aliases, an invalid date,
contradictory aliases, an unrepresented restatement, a quarterly duplicate and
no rejection) through `assembleContextPayload`, and checks against main's
output recorded at f1b2a556: the rejected records and the block's periods and
notes. During development the whole Stage B output, the statement blocks and
the multiples result were also compared by hash with main's and were
identical; those whole-output hashes are not kept as tests, because any later
unrelated change to those outputs would break them. It also shows a reworded duplicate sentence keeps its note and a non-duplicate
rejection worded as a duplicate gets none.

Nothing stored gains a key, per caller of `normalizeQuarterRows` (its result is
unchanged, so this holds for each): compute.ts (`normalizeStatementQuarters`
and its gap `compute.quarterRows.*`, the TTM readers, the projection, DCF and
returns history rows, `rejectedAffectsCurrentWindow`, the fiscal calendar and
fcfHistory lookups), filingDisclosures.ts (currency checks, the fiscal calendar, quarterly
rows and the quarterly trend notes), peers.ts (peer quarter windows and exclusions), capital.ts,
financialMetrics.ts, growth.ts and returns.ts (their period gaps), valuation.ts
(`deriveOwnHistory`'s `rejectedPeriods` and the own-history window gap) and
payload.ts (`annualFiscalLabels` and `realDay`). The FMP family
`rejectedPeriods` (`balanceIntegrity.ts`) come from `statementIntegrityRows`,
not from this function. `normalizeQuarterRowsWithKinds`' result stays inside
`oneRowPerPeriod`, which returns `{ rows, notes }` as before. The test checks
that the Stage B output, the payload and the multiples result (own-history
disclosure) hold no kind word, and that the gap entries carrying a duplicate
sentence (and the own-history window gap) keep their exact keys.

O1. `buildRevenueAnchor` keeps a local `notCovered` array beside the path rows,
set where the gate is decided (`cal.value === null && !cal.staleAgainstReported`,
the branch that writes `<label> is not covered by the fiscal-year estimates`).
The local `stop` object carries `notCovered`: the year's own flag when its
reason is the year's gate, the prior year's when the reason quotes that gate
(`there is no consensus growth into it (year N: <gate>)`), false for the other
four stops. The suffix ` (the estimates cover through ...)` reads it instead of
`/not covered/` over the stop sentence. The path rows, the consensus path and
everything returned are unchanged. Equivalence: the other gates and stops are
built from ISO dates (forecast windows, estimate dates snapped to the fiscal
calendar, the reported-through date, all checked as `YYYY-MM-DD`), numbers and
fixed words, none of which contains `not covered`, so the regex and the flag
agree on every input. `tests/stageB.valuationD65.test.ts` builds through
`buildDcfAssumptions` a direct and a nested not-covered stop, a
stale-against-reported gate, a direct and a nested `consensusGate` gate, the
final-year stop, the floor and re-acceleration stops, the clamped year two and
no consensus, checks the stop clause against main's, that the anchor and its
consensus path rows keep their exact key lists with no `notCovered` key, and
that the suffix appears exactly on the two not-covered cases, where the old
regex matches. The whole assumptions object was compared by hash with main's
during development and was identical; that hash is not kept as a test.

`tests/refusalWording.ratchet.test.ts` unpins payload.ts and valuation.ts, which
read no wording now. Not changed: every decision. The comparison check
(`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80 files) shows no difference; none of its cases has
a rejected duplicate period, so the tests above carry the proof for G7. Left for
later steps: the gap readers G1-G6 (gap entries are stored, so a code there is
a stored-format change), the provider, stored-report and sector-specific
readers, and the identity comparisons.

## D-222 - Refusal codes, step 5: the stock-compensation, cash and share-count rechecks read the code (2026-11-12)

Principle P11. Step 5 of the D-218 migration moves the last four readers of a
D-218 code from the refusal sentence to the code, under the D-219 read rule (a
coded conflict is decided by its code alone, an unknown or unrelated code fails
closed, a conflict without a code is read by its original sentence pattern in
`src/edgar/refusalCauseRead.ts`). Three are in the vendor/SEC comparison
(`admitCashFields`, `src/edgar/financialEnrichment.ts`): the vendor-zero stock
compensation recheck (C1, `priorSbcZero`), the stock-compensation replay (C2,
`replaySbc`) and the cash replay (C3, `replayCash`). The fourth is the
loss-quarter EPS recheck in `guardVendorShareFields` (C13, `canRecheck`,
`src/pipeline/keyless.ts`). Every other condition at the four sites is
unchanged: `usable === false`, the vendor and SEC values, the SEC evidence's
unit, period and single tag, the field and statement tests, and C13's
`reconcileFiled`, quarter and negative-value tests. Nothing else is switched.

| Reader | Field | Codes | Legacy wording (moved verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vendorSecStockCompensation` (C1, C2) | stockBasedCompensation | `vendor-sec-value-conflict` | starts `vendor/SEC stockBasedCompensation conflict:` |
| `vendorSecCash` (C3) | cashAndCashEquivalents (balance rows) | `vendor-sec-value-conflict` | starts `vendor/SEC cashAndCashEquivalents conflict:` |
| `vendorShareRecheck` (C13) | eps, epsDiluted | `vendor-share-value-conflict` | starts `the vendor's ` and includes `; field unavailable until reconciled` |

First, a fix (its own commit). `withPrimaryCapitalBasis`
(`src/pipeline/primaryCapitalBasis.ts`) resolved a refused
commonStockRepurchased conflict by copying it with a new sentence, so it kept
whatever code the old sentence had, which can be `vendor-sec-value-conflict`
(D-219 found this). Now that the code is read, a code must never sit beside a
sentence it was not written with, so the rewritten conflict carries no code;
the old sentence is still tracked by the `superseded` map, which is unchanged.
The resolution is a calculation view: it is not stored in a run input snapshot,
and the payload and audit read only its values, resolution and sentence, so no
stored byte changes. `revenueAdmission.ts` makes the same kind of copy with
`revenue-scope`, a code read before D-218, on revenue only; it is left as it is.
(Revised by D-226: that copy now keeps only `revenue-scope`.)

Why code and wording agree for every current writer. One writer writes
`vendor-sec-value-conflict`: the comparison's refusal branch, which writes the
code with `vendor/SEC ${field} conflict: ...` on the compared field and on its
dependents: cashAndCashEquivalents gives it to cashAndShortTermInvestments and
netDebt, and the beginning and ending cash give it to netChangeInCash.
stockBasedCompensation has no dependents and is nobody's dependent, and
cashAndCashEquivalents is compared only on balance rows and is nobody's
dependent, so on these two fields the code always comes with the field's own
sentence, annual and quarterly. The refusal branch always writes the code, so
the sentence never comes without it. The comparison's other writes on these
fields are usable resolutions or carry their own sentences, without a code. No
other writer composes a `vendor/SEC <field> conflict:` sentence (the operating
cash-flow and income conflicts read `vendor/SEC operating cash-flow conflict at`
and `vendor/SEC conflict for`), and the SEC statement builder's cash withholdings
have other sentences and no code. One writer writes `vendor-share-value-conflict`:
`guardVendorShareFields`, only in its no-split disagreement branch, whose
sentence starts `the vendor's ` and always ends `; field unavailable until
reconciled`. The guard's other sentences on eps/epsDiluted (not a usable
figure, no filed figure, ADR) have no code and do not contain that ending, and
across a split it writes no conflict at all. Nothing copies a conflict onto
these fields from another field. The copies that keep fields (the Stage B views,
`withCashFlowSbcBasis`, run input snapshots) keep code and sentence together;
the release-quarter EPS reconciliation and the share-unit repair write new
conflicts without a code or delete the conflict. The four codes read before
D-218 are written only on revenue, operating income and interest expense.

Snapshots. `CONFLICT_CAUSES_READ_BY_CODE` derives from the readers, so
`captureRunInputSnapshot` now keeps the last two step-1 codes too. Every D-218
code is now read and kept in a new snapshot, so `withoutDualWrittenCauses`
removes nothing today; it and `DUAL_WRITTEN_CONFLICT_CAUSES` stay so that a
later dual-written code is again kept out of snapshots until a reader reads it.
A snapshot or frozen input without codes is read by its sentences, as before.
Nothing else about snapshots changes. No refusal sentence, other writer or
version stamp changes: code and sentence agree on every conflict a current
writer produces, so no decision changes, and conflicts reach no Stage B output,
payload, report or export.

Not changed: every decision. The comparison check (`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80
files) shows no difference. `tests/refusalCause.readers.test.ts` builds each
refusal with the real writers (`admitStockCompensation`, `admitBalanceCash`,
`enrichFinancialFields`, `guardVendorShareFields`), runs each reader on it with
codes and with them deleted, and requires the same outcome. It covers the
vendor-zero and replay stock compensation, the cash replay, loss-quarter EPS on
both fields, and the neighbours each reader must reject: other refusals placed
on the field, the cash dependents, other cash-flow fields, positive EPS, and
the guard's split-check, not-a-usable-figure and no-filed sentences. It also
shows a coded conflict is decided by its code whatever its sentence, and a
conflict without a code by its sentence. Left for later steps: the identity
comparisons (C6, C8, C10, C15, C16, C17) and the gap, provider, stored-report
and sector-specific readers.

## D-221 - Refusal codes, step 4: the combined-total recovery and the minor-difference note read the code (2026-11-12)

Principle P11. Step 4 of the D-218 migration moves two more readers from the
refusal sentence to its typed code, under the D-219 read rule (a coded conflict
is decided by its code alone, an unknown or unrelated code fails closed, a
conflict without a code is read by its original sentence pattern in
`src/edgar/refusalCauseRead.ts`), and moves a third, legacy-only reader there.
All three are in `admitDebtFields` (`src/edgar/financialEnrichment.ts`), on
totalDebt: the gross-debt reconciliation (C7), which lifts a combined-total
refusal when one filing bridges the gross amount to carrying debt; the
minor-difference note (C9), which records a usable, filed-family total's
retained vendor difference as a manifest admission; and the old vendor-sum
guard (C5, `revisitVendorSum`). Every other condition at the three sites is
unchanged: C7's gross bridge and vendor-value check, C9's `usable === true` and
`resolution === "filed-family"` checks, C5's vendor-value and issuer checks.
Nothing else is switched.

| Reader | Field | Codes | Legacy wording (moved verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `combinedAggregateExceedsComponents` (C7) | totalDebt | `debt-combined-aggregate-exceeds-components` | starts `incomplete debt carrying value: same-period DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount ` |
| `debtTotalMinorDifference` (C9) | totalDebt | `debt-total-minor-difference` | starts `vendor total ` and includes `minor difference retained` |
| `legacyVendorSumRefusal` (C5) | totalDebt | none (legacy-only) | `/^incomplete debt carrying value: the vendor lease line .*?, but the vendor total debt .* is not its short-term debt \+ long-term debt \+ lease line, so its composition is unknown;/` |

Why code and wording agree for every current writer. C7: the combined-total
sentence and its code are written together by one helper,
`uncomposedDebtRefusal` (`debtCompleteness.ts`), which picks the code from the
exceeding tag; it is called by the debt admission's cascade and by the SEC
statement builder's (whose `NoteSink.causeOf` keys the code to the exact field
and sentence). Every other tag gets `debt-aggregate-exceeds-components` and a
sentence naming that tag; every other totalDebt sentence starts otherwise
(`DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount` appears only after `current/noncurrent
financing components do not establish the total;`), and a component refusal
wrapped into the total starts `<field> is unavailable (`. A kept prior refusal
keeps its own sentence and code. C9: both writers (`completeFiledDebtScope` and
`completeFromFiling`) write the code only when `minorDebtTotalNote` is not
empty, and the note then always starts `vendor total ` (from
`debtTotalComparison`) and contains `minor difference retained`; with no
difference no conflict is written at all. No other writer puts a usable,
filed-family conflict on totalDebt, and the minor-limit refusal (`... exceeds
the minor-difference limit`) is unusable, carries a lease-line code and lacks
the phrase. C5: no current writer produces the sentence, coded or not: the
only sentences starting with the lease-line lead come from
`completeFromFiling`'s `refuse`, and none of its causes contains `is not its
short-term debt + long-term debt + lease line`; its one `the vendor total
debt` cause reads `is unavailable, so its composition is unknown`. So the
reader's code set is empty: a coded conflict with that sentence is never
revisited, which no current writer can produce, and an older row without a
code is revisited by its sentence as before. The four codes read before D-218
are written only on revenue, operating income and interest expense, and
nothing copies a conflict between those fields and totalDebt; the two copies
that keep a code and change the sentence (`primaryCapitalBasis.ts`,
repurchases; `revenueAdmission.ts`, revenue) never reach it. (Revised by D-222:
the repurchase copy now drops the code.) The only
conflict copied onto a debt field, the vendor/SEC cash conflict on net debt,
keeps both its sentence and its code.

Snapshots. `CONFLICT_CAUSES_READ_BY_CODE` derives from the readers, so
`captureRunInputSnapshot` now also keeps `debt-total-minor-difference`; the
combined-total code was already kept for C11, and the legacy reader adds none.
Two step-1 codes are still removed (`vendor-sec-value-conflict`,
`vendor-share-value-conflict`) and the four earlier codes stay. (Revised by
D-222: they are read and kept too; none is removed.) Nothing else
about snapshots changes. No refusal sentence, writer or version stamp changes:
the code and the sentence agree on every conflict a current writer produces,
so no decision changes, and conflicts still reach no Stage B output, payload,
report or export.

Not changed: every decision. The comparison check (`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80
files) shows no difference. `tests/refusalCause.readers.test.ts` runs every
refusal each reader handles, and the neighbouring ones it must reject (for C7
the other aggregate code; for C9 the completions with no minor difference and
qualifications that are refused, not filed-family or minor-retained), built by
the debt admission and the SEC statement builder, with codes and with them
deleted, and requires the same outcome; it also shows a coded conflict is
decided by its code whatever its sentence and a conflict without a code by its
sentence, and that no coded conflict passes the legacy-only reader. Left for
later steps: C1-C3 and C13 (whose codes are still removed from snapshots), the
identity comparisons and the gap, provider, stored-report and sector-specific
readers. (Revised by D-222: C1-C3 and C13 now read their codes.)

## D-220 - Refusal codes, step 3: the two debt-maturity checks read the code (2026-11-11)

Principle P11. Step 3 of the D-218 migration moves two more readers from the
refusal sentence to its typed code, under the D-219 read rule (a coded conflict
is decided by its code alone, an unknown or unrelated code fails closed, a
conflict without a code is read by its original sentence pattern in
`src/edgar/refusalCauseRead.ts`). Both readers are in `admitDebtFields`
(`src/edgar/financialEnrichment.ts`): the split check (`splitRefusal`, C4),
which lets a refused maturity-bucket split leave an inclusive LongTermDebt
total standing, and the same-filing debt-note recovery
(`recoverNoteCarryingDebt`, C12). Every other condition at both sites is
unchanged, including C12's `fiscalStandIn` gate. Nothing else is switched.

Readers, by field (one code has two sentences, so the readers are per field):

| Reader | Field | Codes | Legacy wording (moved verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shortTermDebtMaturityScope` (C4 and C12) | shortTermDebt | `debt-maturity-scope` | starts `debt maturity scope unresolved:` |
| `longTermDebtNoncurrentAllocation` (C4) | longTermDebt | `debt-noncurrent-allocation` | starts `noncurrent carrying debt allocation unavailable:` |

Why code and wording agree for every current writer. On shortTermDebt the only

stamp changes: the code and the sentence agree on every conflict a current
writer produces, so no decision changes, and conflicts still reach no Stage B
output, payload, report or export.

## D-219 - Refusal codes, step 2: the lease and debt-recovery checks read the code (2026-11-11)

Principle P11. Step 2 of the D-218 migration moves two readers from the
refusal sentence to its typed code. Both decide whether a refused total debt
may be revisited: the D-186 lease-portion recovery
(`restoreRefusedOperatingPortion`, `src/pipeline/stageB/leaseScope.ts`, C14)
and the same-filing debt completion (`completeFiledDebtScope`,
`src/edgar/financialEnrichment.ts`, C11). Nothing else is switched.

Read rule (owner-directed; revises D-218). A conflict that carries a code is
decided by the code alone: it passes only if the code is in that reader's set,
so an unknown or unrelated code fails closed and the sentence is not read. A
conflict without a code (a frozen input, an older run snapshot, the same-report
cases, or a writer that writes none) is read by its sentence with the reader's
original pattern, moved verbatim. Those patterns live in one module,
`src/edgar/refusalCauseRead.ts`, marked as the only place a conflict without a
code is read by its wording; nothing is added there except when a reader is
migrated. A code is still never derived from a sentence or written onto a row
that has none.

Code sets. C14: `debt-lease-line-no-operating-total`. C11:
`debt-lease-line-refused`, `debt-lease-line-no-operating-total`,
`debt-vendor-short-term-zero`, `debt-aggregate-exceeds-components`,
`debt-combined-aggregate-exceeds-components`. Every current writer of a sentence
either pattern matches writes a code in that set (the lease-line refusals, the
vendor short-term zero and the tagged-total check); the only other sentence
they match is the pre-18ea3137 vendor-sum refusal, which has no writer and is
read by wording. The identity comparisons beside both readers (C10, C15) are
unchanged.

Snapshots. `captureRunInputSnapshot` now keeps these five codes, so a run that
computes Stage B from its snapshot decides by them; the seven step-1 codes no
reader reads are still removed, and the four earlier codes stay. (Revised by
D-220: the four debt-maturity codes are kept too; three are still removed.
Revised by D-221: and the minor-difference code; two are still removed.
Revised by D-222: and the last two; none is removed.) No version
stamp changes: the code and the sentence agree on every conflict a current
writer produces, so no decision changes, and conflicts still reach no Stage B
output, payload, report or export.

Not changed: every decision. The comparison check (`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80
files) shows no difference. `tests/refusalCause.readers.test.ts` runs every
refusal each reader handles, and every debt refusal it does not, with its codes
and with them deleted, and requires the same outcome both ways. Left for later
steps: C1-C4, C7, C9, C12, C13 and the gap, provider, stored-report and
sector-specific readers. (Revised by D-220: C4 and C12 now read
their codes. Revised by D-221: C7 and C9 too, and C5 is legacy-only.
Revised by D-222: and C1-C3 and C13.) Found while checking: the primary cash-flow repurchase
resolution (`primaryCapitalBasis.ts`) copies a coded vendor/SEC conflict and
replaces its sentence, keeping the code; no reader uses that code yet, and it
must be fixed before a reader of `vendor-sec-value-conflict` moves to codes.
(Revised by D-222: fixed; the rewritten conflict carries no code.)

## D-218 - Refusal codes beside refusal sentences, step 1: write, do not read (2026-11-11)

Principle P11: a refusal is judged from its cause and evidence, never its
wording. Admission status still travels as English in `StatementFieldConflict.reason`
and `ManifestEntry.reason`, and later code decides by matching that text. A scan
of `src` finds 69 such lines in 51 decision sites: 17 read field-conflict
sentences in Stage A or Stage B (debt, cash, stock compensation, vendor EPS), 7
read gap sentences at run time, 9 read provider status sentences, 17 read the
stored sentences of a saved report (one of them, the non-bank lender convention,
is sector-specific) and 1 reads an estimate-anchor sentence for display. The
rule-consolidation review proposed typed causes with a ban on reason parsing;
its critique made two conditions binding: extend the existing typed fields
rather than start a second cause system, and migrate in steps (write codes
beside the prose, move readers one at a time, then ban the parsing), never
guessing a cause for a legacy row that has none.

Options: rewrite each reader to a code in one change (changes outcomes for
every frozen input and saved row without a code); infer codes from the existing
sentences (the parsing this replaces); or write a code where each sentence is
composed and change no reader. Choice: the third. `STATEMENT_CONFLICT_CAUSES`
(`src/types/refusalCause.ts`) is the one list; `StatementFieldConflict.cause`
takes it, keeping its four existing members. Twelve new codes are written
beside the unchanged sentences by the writers that compose them:
`admitDebtFields`, the lease-line and same-filing completions, the stock
compensation and cash comparison, the SEC statement builder's debt
withholdings and `guardVendorShareFields`. Each code is chosen by the branch
that wrote the sentence, never by reading it; a total refused because of a
refused component takes the component's code only when that component carries
one. No reader uses the new codes. (Revised by D-219: two readers now do.
Revised by D-220: four do. Revised by D-221: six do. Revised by D-222: every
new code is read.)

Kept out of outputs: conflicts never reach Stage B output, the payload, the
report or its exports, so nothing a report shows or stores changes.
`captureRunInputSnapshot` removes the new codes (`DUAL_WRITTEN_CONFLICT_CAUSES`)
so a new run snapshot keeps the bytes it would have had; the four existing
codes stay. (Revised by D-219: snapshots now keep the five codes
those readers read. Revised by D-220: and the four debt-maturity codes.
Revised by D-221: and the minor-difference code. Revised by D-222: and the
last two, so none is removed.) `ManifestEntry` gets no code in this step: gap entries are copied
into Stage B output, the payload, `appendix.missingData` (strict schema),
`fairValue.reasons` and snapshots, and keeping a code out of all of them is a
larger change than this step. The G and P gap readers therefore stay
wording-only for now. (Revised by D-223: G7, which reads rejection sentences in
memory, not a gap entry, now reads a typed rejection kind.)

Not changed: every decision. The comparison check (`golden:diff`, 10 cases, 80
files) shows no difference. Sites that compare two refusal sentences for
identity (whether a netDebt refusal is the totalDebt one) need a link between
the two refusals, not a code, and are left as they are. One reader
(`financialEnrichment.ts`, the old vendor-sum wording) matches a sentence no
current writer produces; it reads only rows built before 18ea3137 and needs a
legacy rule of its own. (Revised by D-221: it is a legacy-only reader in
`refusalCauseRead.ts`, with no codes.) Sector-specific readers and writers are untouched and
left for an owner decision.

Guard: `tests/refusalWording.ratchet.test.ts` pins the wording-reading lines
per file, so a new one fails and a migrated one must be unpinned.
`tests/refusalCause.dualWrite.test.ts` checks, on every conflict its shapes
produce, that each code and the wording its reader matches agree both ways,
that every new code is reached, that an uncoded legacy component leaves its
total uncoded, and that a snapshot drops the new codes but keeps the old ones.
A later step that moves a reader to a code must also stop removing that code
from snapshots, with its own snapshot note, and decide how a frozen input or
saved row with no code is read. (Revised by D-219: by its sentence, through one
module, and never assigned a code.)

## D-217 - Stamp new reports with their evidence rules; never rewrite old ones (2026-11-10)

Principle P21. A saved report had no field saying which evidence rules built
it; readers guessed from `meta.specVersion` and `meta.pipelineVersion` text
(`specVersionBefore`). The rule review proposed a stamp on new reports and one
note on old ones (rule-consolidation report, "Saved reports"); its critique
kept that, with two conditions: readers accept the stamp before the writer
emits it, and the note never replaces a specific currency, scope or legacy
warning.

Options: migrate stored reports to add a stamp (rewrites stored meaning, breaks
P21); infer the rules from the spec text (the guess this replaces); or an
optional stamp written only on new reports. Choice: optional
`meta.evidenceContract`, owned by `src/report/evidenceContract.ts`
(`EVIDENCE_CONTRACT_VERSION = "EVIDENCE_CONTRACT_1"`). The report schema, and
so both read modes of the stored-report reader, accept any non-empty string up
to 128 characters; `assembleReport` and `buildDataOnlyReport` write the
current value. Linking a recovered verify artifact keeps that artifact's own
stamp or its absence, as it keeps its spec and pipeline versions.

Stored reports are not migrated and their bytes do not change. A report with
no stamp shows "Built under older rules: this report has no evidence-rules
stamp, so its figures are shown as saved." One whose stamp this
build does not know (for example one written by a newer build) shows "Built
under unrecognised rules: this report's evidence-rules stamp "…" is not one
this app knows, so its figures are shown as saved." It is neither refused
nor treated as current. `evidenceContractNotice` (presentation layer, P22)
derives the note once; the app header notices, the Markdown header and the
print header show it after the synthetic and provider-fallback notices
(Revised by D-225: the audit export's header block now shows it too). Every
existing specific warning is unchanged.

The report spec stays 1.73.0: like `presumedCostUsd`, this adds an optional
meta field and changes no figure, and moving the spec would change the
Versions row of every new report. The stamp moves only by a later decision;
nothing bumps it automatically. Out of scope: freezing the legacy adapters,
`specVersionBefore` and its cutoffs, replays or reruns.

Evidence: `golden:diff` over 10 cases and 80 files differs only in
`meta.evidenceContract` in each rebuilt `report.json` and, because it hashes
the whole report, the dossier's `data-report-identity` attribute. The audit
fixture's one new delta is `report.meta.evidenceContract`. The bundled samples
(`DEMO-sample.json`, `DEMO-current.json`) predate the stamp and are not
stamped, so they now show the older-rules note. The catalyst/risk export
snapshot (an unstamped legacy fixture) changes only by that note: with the
note line removed, its Markdown and print hashes equal the earlier snapshot.

## D-216 - Saved reports that carry a field no released build wrote (2026-11-09)

Principle P21. Saved reports #59 (QCOM, spec 1.23.1) and #60 (FIGR, spec 1.23.2)
stopped opening: both carry `filingDisclosures.corporateActionBridge`, which the
strict report schema rejects as an unknown key. Git history shows the field only
in a stash ("Preserved local work before main update", 2026-11-01, on base
65ed5638), so uncommitted local work wrote it on 2026-11-01 and it never
reached main. Everything else in both reports passes the strict schema.

Options: add the field to the report schema (new reports could then carry it
too, and its feature would need porting); accept unknown fields on read (hides
corruption everywhere); or list each retired field once and set it aside on
read. Choice: `src/report/legacyRetiredFields.ts` lists a retired field by exact
path, a frozen copy of the shape it was written with, and the exact spec stamps
of the builds that wrote it (1.23.1, 1.23.2 and 1.23.3). Only a match on all
three is set aside; any other unknown field, shape or stamp (including empty,
malformed, pre-release and out-of-range stamps) still fails the read. The view adds a
fixed-wording filing note saying what is not shown: the record's table and
source excerpts. It says the form, accession, filing date and link remain in
the filing notes only when one note states all four for every item; otherwise it
says the source list is not shown either. Stored
bytes are not changed and the feature is not ported. No other saved report and
no new report changes.

## D-215 - Restore corroborated operating evidence without relaxing grades (2026-11-08)

Revised by D-262: a compatible directly filed interest-expense fact settles a conflicting vendor observation before the capitalized-borrowing-cost guard; without that expense proof, the scope refusal remains.

The DHI audit reproduced a revenue-scope admission error: a quarterly primary
statement established operating sales, but the issuer policy then rejected the
same broadly named SEC revenue concept across history. Inherit a concept's
operating scope only from matching filed amounts, duration, currency and filing;
a contradictory retained sales presentation prevents broad-concept promotion.

Restoring revenue exposed a separate provider interest-classification problem.
Interest incurred and capitalized into inventory, and inventory interest later
released to cost of sales, cannot be summed as financing expense or used for a
synthetic credit rating. Historical borrowing-cost evidence must bind its own
period to the corresponding debt balances and retain explicit qualifications.
Never reconstruct a missing expense or ownership allocation from a residual.

Annual guidance and quarterly earnings schedules require explicit scope in the
source; recognized rows do not authorize arbitrary dates or unparsed metrics.
Keep evidence floors, source conflicts and historical reports unchanged. The
new report/payload/Stage B/pipeline stamps identify changed semantics; no band
threshold or valuation-target adjustment is introduced. See the
[audit and verification record](https://github.com/eligorelick/Metis/blob/bda87e4c0b575fdf4af2a4e31a66854c9c42337b/docs/audit/2026-11-08-dhi-report-4.md).

## D-214 - Quarterly evidence propagation and reader consistency (2026-11-07)

A fresh review after D-213 found five integration/admission defects that the
earlier tests and reviews missed. Corrected quarterly EPS/shares now enter both
Stage B and the model/verifier payload with their SEC provenance and conflict
history. Direct release values require complete split coverage and a canonical
factor of one from their filing basis to the report basis. An accounting context
date cannot establish the first adjusted trading session. Uncertain timing or a
non-unit factor preserves the existing row rather than inventing an adjustment.

Both annual-geography readers refuse nil facts and transformations other than
their supported dot-decimal formats. Explicitly referenced annual product and
available geography rows remain visible beside quarterly UI tables, with dates
and allocation qualifications. Print table citations use structured canonical
destinations rather than rediscovering URLs from parenthesized prose.

These are bounded correctness repairs, not a revised investment thesis. No
forecast premium, score threshold or base valuation formula changes. Report
1.71.0, payload 1.90.0 and Stage B `STAGE_B_2026_11_RELEASE_SPLIT_SAFETY_64`
identify the changed admission/context semantics; historical reports and source
snapshots retain their original bytes. Pipeline and evidence-selection versions
remain unchanged because prompts and pass algorithms did not change. See the
[review and validation record](2026-11-07-evidence-backed-report-remediation.md#post-merge-review-and-integration-follow-up).

## D-213 - Evidence-backed report remediation (2026-11-07)

Choose general source/period repairs and additive sensitivities over a company-
specific upward valuation adjustment. Commercial opportunities deserve evidence
coverage, but undisclosed profits, adoption or consensus inclusion cannot safely
be filled with optimistic assumptions. Preserve source conflicts, accounting
scope, historical report bytes, existing base formulas and score thresholds.

The additional tax/capital grid isolates mechanical dependence on those inputs;
it is not a newly underwritten forecast. Broader normalization and SOTP require
item-specific tax and segment economics. Supplemental numerical coverage is
reported as an explicit unchecked inventory rather than inflated verification.
This adds evidence and disclosure complexity but reduces the risk of false
precision. [Audit dispositions and validation](2026-11-07-evidence-backed-report-remediation.md)
record remaining evidence limits and distinguish frozen replay from a new full run.

Final Node 24 `npm run verify` passed: both complete coverage runs passed
17,014 tests across 745 files with three existing skips each; four integration
tests, typecheck, lint, build and dependency checks passed, with zero known
vulnerabilities. Independent task and whole-branch review findings, including
the final accounting-scope edge case, were fixed and re-reviewed. Original
real-run files and historical synthetic baselines remain unchanged.

## D-141 - FIG report source reconciliation and qualified evidence (2026-11-01)

- **Evidence and choice.** The completed FIG report's historical EPS and weighted-share fields conflict with direct retained SEC facts even though no split was recorded. Extend the existing refusal boundary to exact issuer, period, currency and ordinary-share comparisons; retain vendor values and filed evidence as conflicts. Do not silently substitute a different common-earnings allocation or use missing primary coverage as evidence of error. Matching current observations remain admitted. The measured FIG annual share trend and its sole leadership score input become unavailable.
- **Report integrity.** Derive price-to-SMA relations from stored indicators while keeping the house trend category; distinguish quote/computed range sources, forecast periods from the estimate envelope date, and full-weight from applicable-weight coverage. Form 4 P/S counts include private transactions. Correct the compound-title pseudo-person and listed-as title-check bypass. Qualify the known provider-only earnings date in relevant prose, retain the original text in the audit, and keep affected claim support unchecked.
- **Guidance.** Admit compact currency ranges only in an unambiguous dated outlook context. Preserve quarterly versus annual scope and non-GAAP basis; combined headings, mixed currencies and unreadable ranges refuse. A failed extraction does not establish absence of issuer guidance.
- **Compatibility and cost.** Report spec 1.55.0, payload 1.59.0, Stage B 38, pipeline 1.6.17 and current-report parser 1.2.2 identify the new behavior. Old input snapshots require their original engine; normal resumes rebuild inputs and compare payload identity. Linking an already verified report preserves its original method stamps while settling the ledger. It is not new research under current methods. No historical report or cost is rewritten, and no additional inference is required by these repairs.
- **Validation contract.** Failing-first production-suite regressions and offline frozen FIG replay cover these changes. The historical comparison changes only its report stamp and technical trend sentence beyond earlier reviewed deltas; financial pins remain exact. Live future output quality, vendor data accuracy, investment judgments and forecast realization are not established by these tests.

## D-140 - Current-main report integrity and bounded recovery (2026-11-01)

- **Baseline and alternatives.** Start at upstream `4ec0368ae8b17a8d4c8dc6fc1d2a862c2b92bddc`, not the original checkout that was 760 commits behind. Preserve current source-bound receivables, financial conflict refusal, request settlement, generation validation, section-writer evidence and historical reader conventions. Older overlapping replacements are superseded; the original dirty workspace remains recoverable.
- **Evidence and arithmetic.** Nearby fiscal endpoints collapse only with explicit matching issuer, currency, fiscal scope and compatible filing metadata. Conflicting scope or field-source recency prevents whole-row selection. Refused recent cash flow cannot be replaced with older burn quarters. Retained FIGR filing facts independently check Q2 2026 CFO of -35.151M and Q4 2025 CFO of +13.271M; existing conflict admission remains intact. Share-price prose supplies its unit only under the narrow verified parser rule. DCF formulas, grade thresholds, and source reconciliation are unchanged.
- **Recovery and cost.** Synthesis uses subset prompts with a six-launch allowance per case order and explicit generation, shared by automatic retries/restarts. Valid sections retain their digests and actual writer provenance. A billed or uncertain transport failure never replays the original request automatically. Proven pre-send failures retain free bounded retries; resumed input is checked using the existing D-121 policy. Advisory task pacing is distinct from hard limits. No provider completion guarantee is made.
- **Outcome and compatibility.** Mandatory bull, bear, synthesis and verification stages must succeed (or have explicitly covered durable reuse) before the new optional completion marker says complete. Final validation can still withhold that marker. Process termination, workflow completion and the scope of verified claims remain separate. Cost provenance joins exact attempt IDs. Historical schemas remain readable and no saved report is rewritten.
- **Stamps and regression evidence.** Report 1.54.0, payload 1.56.0, Stage B 35 and pipeline stage-c-1.6.14 invalidate reuse across changed generation/calculation conventions. Financial method stamps and score bands stay fixed. The canonical payload fixture changes only its version: an exact fingerprint/byte assertion restores 1.55.0 in memory before every older golden check. The audit comparison changes only `report.meta.specVersion`; all other financial/provenance pins remain enforced. New source modules join the existing risk coverage inventory without lowering thresholds.
- **Limits.** Offline fixtures and mocked providers establish regression behavior, not successful live QCOM/FIGR generation. Full earnings normalization, capital reconciliation and paid reruns are deferred. Verified batches, remaining release gates and merge-history checks are recorded in [the integration checkpoint](https://github.com/eligorelick/Metis/blob/bda87e4c0b575fdf4af2a4e31a66854c9c42337b/docs/audit/2026-11-01-current-main-integration.md).

## D-139 - Prospective measurement and report reliability (2026-10-31)

- **Decision and alternatives.** Extend the existing offline report evaluator with a predeclared study, deadline-bound registrations, full-cohort evaluation and paired baselines. A second calculation engine would duplicate measurement rules. Reweighting production grades without outcomes would invent calibration. No model calls, network requests, trading actions or database writes are introduced.
- **Admission and custody.** Study files use exclusive writes, verified content hashes and portable hashed slot filenames. Missing registrations and outcomes remain in the denominator; invalid actuals are excluded with reasons. Local receipts are unwitnessed, and supplied identities, sectors, accounting bases, source availability and lifecycle coverage remain operator assertions. The strict V2 guard remains closed until a producer binds complete measurement dimensions. Operating EPS is not accepted as GAAP diluted EPS.
- **Measurement.** Group descriptive errors by sector, metric, scenario, unit, currency, basis, exact report/registration horizons, period length, full/partial period, pipeline and method version, and baseline. Retain row-level observations, missingness and percentage-error denominator counts. Market total returns, including supplied delisting losses, remain separate observations; present DCF value is not a future-price forecast. No significance, forecast accuracy, calibrated grade or investment recommendation follows from tests or synthetic examples.
- **Grades.** Shared app/Markdown/print diagnostics use the recorded applicable coverage and score for a conditional missing-input range. Unknown coverage remains unknown; explicit null coverage is route-inapplicable. Recorded grades, weights and financial formulas stay unchanged. The range assumes missing applicable signal weight can score anywhere from zero to 100; it does not measure factual error, model validity or future performance.
- **Valuation and timing.** Robustness requires complete, unique two-axis modeled grids. Actual observed crossings remain evidence of sensitivity even if a grid is missing. A pure reader guard withholds unsupported saved robustness claims without rewriting report files. Timing text distinguishes contemporaneous capture, later-published/acquired evidence and unverified timing; acquisition alone cannot certify historical source availability.
- **Compatibility evidence.** The historical fixture delta changes only its scenario-presentation object to reflect incomplete-grid refusal. One exact sensitivity-scope sentence is restored in memory before the unchanged complete payload, financial and provenance pins. No historical fixture bytes or financial goldens are refreshed. Report 1.53, payload 1.55 and Stage B 34 stay unchanged; these are presentation and evaluation changes, not a new financial method.

**Execution rulings, 2026-10-30:** built on `222f92a` (B4a, PR #76), in parallel with B5a. Otherwise exclude that year's proxy and dollars from measured timing coverage and name it. Owner decision (delegated, 2026-10-27): adopted as recommended. Extends D-68's unpriced-year rule and D-61's fiscal-year benchmark, informed by Dittmar and Field (2015), *Can managers time the market?* Seven days is a house tolerance, not a result from the paper; extending the provider history remains deferred.

## D-73 (debt completeness, 2026-10-16) Withhold partial debt instead of publishing an understated enterprise value

- **Evidence:** A current quarterly EDGAR balance selected a maturity-schedule amount as short-term debt while long-term carrying debt was absent. Adding leases produced a partial total that understated financing debt. The filing's debt note and aggregate XBRL debt evidence conflicted with that construction. Gross principal, maturity schedules and carrying values are different measures and cannot substitute for one another without reconciliation.
- **Choice:** Preserve a refusal when the available debt components do not establish a complete carrying-value balance. Do not fill the refused amount from a partial vendor row or an older balance sheet. Withhold dependent metrics through the existing missing-data path. Complete balances and evidenced zero debt remain eligible. Extension-tag carrying-value extraction is outside this bounded correction; missing data remains visible.
- **Filed debt presentation:** QCOM's [June 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/804328/000080432826000086/qcom-20260628.htm) places $12.781B of long-term debt below current liabilities, alongside $2.489B of current debt. Subtracting current maturities again understates the $15.270B carrying total. Bind the exact issuer, accession, dates, currency, scale and columns, and reconcile both current-liability subtotals and full liability totals before applying the filed noncurrent scope. Genuinely inclusive tags retain the subtraction. The supported two-column USD grammar is deliberately narrow; unsupported statements establish no override. Normal acquisition and immutable Stage B/payload admission share the same rule.
- **Versions and preservation:** Report `1.19.2`, payload `1.24.2`, Stage B `STAGE_B_2026_10_DEBT_COMPLETENESS_1`. Prior saved reports, snapshots and analyst artifacts retain their original meaning and cannot resume as equivalent. The complete-debt DEMO projection changes its report-version leaf and adds the float measurement date; all financial values remain pinned. Original analysis and recovery artifacts are retained. New paid analyses require the corrected input context, rather than relabeling old-context work.
- **Float scope:** A dated public-float estimate must not be divided by a differently dated outstanding count or rendered as an impossible percentage above 100%. Keep the measurement and its date visible, withhold the incompatible percentage and its use as a current short-interest denominator, and leave valuation shares unchanged. Legacy reports remain readable; the optional float date preserves new reports' source context.
- **Review boundaries:** Late balance and payload admission require the requested ticker's independently confirmed SEC identity and matching numeric, padded and company-facts CIKs; an FMP-supplied CIK alone does not establish the issuer. An unusable debt or lease component cannot prove a total complete, and a rejected fiscal maturity bucket cannot reduce long-term debt. Normal annual Item 8/15 acquisition retains the bounded pre-notes statements alongside its notes, allowing the advertised 10-K presentation proof to operate. Regression controls retain valid mappings, explicit current/noncurrent carrying debt, raw rejected observations, source periods and the existing text cap.
- **Release gates:** Focused debt/refusal regressions, complete and zero-debt controls, the combined local verify gate, independent review and fresh required remote CI remain gates. The preceding Windows export-test follow-up changes only explicit I/O test deadlines, preserving assertions and application source.

Format: `D-nn (WSn) Title` → Options / Risks / Choice / Why / Disclosure.

## D-72 (PR review, 2026-10-16) Preserve the source and withhold unsupported financial history

- **Status:** Implementation, targeted independent rechecks and the complete local gate are finished. Fresh required remote CI remains the release gate.
- **Evidence:** PR #20 identified nine reproducible boundary issues: merged EX-99.2 financial values lost their originating exhibit, zero-padded exhibits and earnings amendments were omitted, quarterly disclosures bypassed whole-row restatement selection, old reporting currencies suppressed current release facts, missing analyst buckets became zeros, undisclosed interest became zero forecast expense, tagged acquisition cash could be counted twice, and a historical residual could be renamed as a new segment. An earlier push's Windows job also exceeded a five-second test deadline while starting two independently bounded real CLI processes; the PR-triggered rerun passed.

Implicit dollars bind to their own release or periodic-filing reporting period; prior currencies cannot be relabeled current. Forecast EPS needs evidenced interest or a matching debt-free balance without contradictory financing components. Keep existing financial grades and thresholds.
- **Amendment boundaries:** Linked Item 9.01 amendments require an exact nonempty SEC event date and inspected earnings scope. Readable unrelated or explicitly non-changing amendments retain the original; unknown/unreadable relevant scope withholds stale substitution. Reporting-period order controls current releases and narratives, including legacy arrays; amendments of older quarters cannot displace the latest quarter. Outlooks for a completed fiscal year are not current guidance.
- **Financial boundaries:** A matching generic acquisition tag can be an aggregate containing a tagged second business payment; it does not prove additivity. A competing nonzero classified acquisitions line leaves the second payment unallocated, with a separate numeric record and partial-coverage warning. Segment residuals require same-presentation filing evidence; cross-filing duration subtraction cannot satisfy that requirement. Unknown interest and unsupported historical residuals remain withheld.
- **Versions:** Report `1.19.1`, payload `1.24.1`, Stage B `STAGE_B_2026_10_NVDA_AUDIT_3`. Prior saved reports and payload artifacts retain their original meaning and cannot resume as equivalent. The audited DEMO comparison changes only the report-version leaf and disclosure currency-basis wording; every financial value remains pinned.

Acquisition context is now $1.535B on the classified vendor line plus a $13B filed payment whose overlap remains unresolved, rather than an unsupported $14.535B total. The known Groq payment stays visible. This is a candidate calculation comparison over retained parsed inputs, not a rerun of exhibit ingestion or a replacement of the original D-71 model output. No provider calls or historical-report writes were made.
- **CI test boundary:** Keep each CLI subprocess's 20-second hard limit and give the enclosing test the sum of its child limits plus five seconds of overhead.
