Revises METHODOLOGY "D&A from separate lines (B-7)", the tagSynonyms header ("the first tag present for the period wins", now "unless it is below a component the line item declares"), the FFO stand-in's stated error direction (the comment on `GENERIC_IMPAIRMENT_TAGS` in `src/pipeline/stageB/financialMetrics.ts`; D-31 itself, "always approximate" with no guaranteed error bound, is unchanged) and the bank interest-income pin in `tests/edgar.statements.test.ts`. Sources: the us-gaap definitions of `DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization`, `DepreciationAndAmortization`, `Depreciation` and the two R&D elements, as the plan quotes them.
- **OD-5. Derived fourth quarters and year-to-date differences on one presentation (FIN-511, FIN-511-V2), with conflict C-9.** Chosen: every quarter derived by subtraction (the year less the nine-month year to date, a year to date less the previous one, the year less three quarters) is paired by one helper, `oneBasisPair` (`src/edgar/presentationLineage.ts`), which the statement builder and `financialEnrichment.filedFlow` both call:
  - The newest copy of the minuend counts as re-filed only when it is not the first-reported copy, carries a different value and is not an amendment (review sharpening 2: an amended 10-K keeps its corrected figure). A minuend that is not re-filed, or whose subtrahend moved with it (review sharpening 1: a re-presentation sequenced through a 10-Q and then the 10-K, SEC FRM 13110.4), keeps today's pair.
  - C-9: a re-filed minuend whose subtrahend did not move with it gives the quarter as first reported only for a re-filing within 1% or a re-presentation the re-filing labels with a discontinued-operations line. A material, unlabelled re-filing withholds the quarter, naming both filings and the move, because a corrected figure replaces the original (ASC 250-10-45-23; this agrees with B6 OD-9) and companyfacts cannot tell a correction from an unlabelled re-presentation. A first-reported copy with no subtrahend filed on or before it is withheld too.
  - OD-5 (a2′): a material, unlabelled re-filing of a subtrahend made after the minuend's filing withholds the quarter in the same way; the later copy is still never netted (D-13). This revises the D-13 pin in `tests/edgar.statements.test.ts` (now "withholds the quarter when a LATER filing restated the year-to-date figure and labels no re-presentation"). The plan expected no census figure to move; in the replay this rule withholds 5 census cells (American Tower's common and net dividends for Q2 2024, Alphabet's buybacks for Q3 2025, Oracle's common and net stock issuance for Q2 FY2026) and AEP's income taxes paid for Q2 2025 among the filers without a snapshot, none in a Stage B window.
  - Rule (b): a quarter is also withheld when the minuend's filing re-presented earlier periods of the concept (a copy moved by more than 1% from the copy filed just before it; only an amendment is excused for its own year) and a filing that supplies a subtrahend did not.
  - A presentation withholding ends the field in every chain: no narrower synonym, stand-in (cash interest paid for interest expense) or derivation (consolidated profit for profit attributable to the parent, derived EBIT for a filed operating income) serves it. The exception is a combined synonym that the component floor would skip as a subset line: it gives way to the next synonym (B13 final review M-6). It is judged against each floor tag by the filings that carry both tags for the periods the quarter nets, as a withheld floor tag is, and by its as-filed derived quarter only against a floor tag no filing carries beside it (final re-review N-1).
  - A derived EBIT whose adjustment or optional interest part is withheld for presentation is itself withheld, quoting that reason, when the derivation uses that operand. An operand it does not use never refuses the EBIT (B13 final review I-1), and is resolved quietly for its disclosure only: a component inside a `NonoperatingIncomeExpense` aggregate that served, a not-in-base tag (an equity-method result beside a pretax element measured before it), or interest the B-39/FIN-508 nesting leaves out beside a served aggregate (the withheld tag is `InterestExpenseNonoperating`, or another filing tags the period's interest that way). An adjustment filed in another currency or period never becomes a withholding beside a published EBIT: beside the aggregate it is named as already inside it, and otherwise it is not subtracted and is named in the error band with why (M-3).
  - Rejected: netting a later re-presented nine-month copy (it can carry a further event); keeping the mixed pair for a small re-filing; the first-reported pair for every material re-filing (the reviewed rule before C-9: a correction supersedes that copy); reading net-income invariance as a label (a classification error leaves net income unchanged too); withholding every quarter whose year was re-filed; the planner's first draft (switch on any re-filing, which regressed a 10-Q-sequenced re-presentation and a 10-K/A).
  - Revises D-13 ("one filing lineage" now means one presentation, filing-date lineage being the minimum) and `src/edgar/statements.ts` invariant 3. Sources: ASC 250-10-45-23 (PwC Viewpoint 30.7); ASC 205-20-45-3 and 45-3A (Deloitte Roadmap 7.3); the SEC's EDGAR API documentation (companyfacts carries only facts that apply to the entire filing entity, so a restatement-axis label does not reach it); SEC FRM 13110.3, 13110.4 and 13210.1; D-13.
- **OD-6. Quarterly growth across a re-presentation (FIN-511-V1).** Chosen: a cell is computed on the basis of the quarter it is printed beside. Where the comparison quarter was re-presented by a filing newer than the printed quarter's own and the printed quarter was not, the cell divides by the comparison's first-reported copy when that copy was filed on or before the printed quarter's filing and is positive, with a note naming it and the re-presenting filing (Bank of America Q3 FY2025 QoQ: 28,088 / 26,463 = +6.1%); otherwise it is a dash. Where the printed quarter was re-presented and its comparison has no copy on the new basis, the cell is a dash with a note. Where the printed quarter's own filing re-presented earlier periods and the filing supplying the comparison did not (rule (b) on the pair, read from the row's `revenuePresentation` marker), the cell is a dash with a note. Every other cell is unchanged, FMP-route rows keep plain arithmetic, and a dashed cell registers no payload figure. O-1 keeps this after C-9: a rate on the printed quarter's own filed basis publishes no superseded level. Rejected: first-reported growth everywhere (the row would not reconcile); a dash everywhere (it would blank year-over-year cells for up to two years under FRM 13110.4). Revises D-13 (extended from the derived quarter to the growth cells) and the trend-table note, whose one-presentation sentence appears only where the check ran (`quarterlyTrendPresentationChecked`, Task 9b). Sources: FRM 13110.4; D-13.
- **FIN-508 (no owner decision).** B-39 is keyed on the period, not on the interest tag that served: when any filing tags the period's interest as `InterestExpenseNonoperating`, the interest is inside the aggregate and is not added back (DQC_0181), even when that tag's quarter is itself withheld for presentation. The "this cannot be checked" caveat (`EBIT_AGGREGATE_MAY_HOLD_INTEREST`) is now carried only where interest is added back beside the aggregate, that is where no filing tags the period's interest that way.
- **FIN-507-V1 (no owner decision).** The derived EBIT's pretax operand reads the same chain as `incomeBeforeTax` (`INCOME_BEFORE_TAX_SPEC`): the filed total, else the B-32 domestic + foreign composition, a mechanical extension of B-32; the disclosure says when the composition was taken as the full total.
- **FIN-510-V2 and FIN-511-V2: shared predicates (no owner decision).** The FFO stand-in calls the builder's floor predicate (`belowComponentFloor`) with the same allowance, and the vendor enrichment calls the builder's pairing helper with the same label test, so a derived value means the same thing on both paths. The enrichment's texts call a derived SEC value "derived", with its period and its two filings, and a vendor figure that a withheld pair leaves unverified is disclosed in one info entry per field.
- **Ruling B: the vendor allowance for a derived SEC value (FIN-511-V2; controller ruling of 2026-10-29, revising A-11 for derived values only).** For a derived SEC value, a vendor figure agrees within max(A-11's allowance, min(the sum over the operands of half each operand's rounding unit, 1% of the larger figure)). An operand's rounding unit is the largest power of ten up to 1,000,000 that divides it exactly; a zero gives 1 and a figure with a fraction gives 0. The operands are the filed copies the compared figure nets: two, or four for short-term sales plus maturities, which can reach 2,000,000 before the cap. A directly filed value keeps A-11 unchanged. AEP's FY2024 operating cash flow, re-rounded from 6,804.3M to 6,804.0M, less nine months of 5,076.9M gives 1,727.1M, which a vendor 1,727.4M now matches (0.55M of operand rounding). The rule covers the enrichment's cash-flow and lease comparisons; the income-classification check still uses A-11 alone (routed to R1a Task 25). Why: a figure the filing states only to the million is uncertain by half a million, and the 1% cap keeps A-11's bound, so 2M against 1M, a zero against a nonzero figure and a sign change stay conflicts.
- **Bank of America's fair value.** Task 7 withholds BAC's Q4 2025 revenue, pretax income and tax under rule (b), because the 10-K of 2026-02-25 re-presented earlier periods and the 10-Q of 2025-10-31 that supplies the nine months did not. Main's existing whole-row TTM revenue gate (`revenueCount < 4` in `src/pipeline/compute.ts`) then drops the trailing twelve months, so the excess-return model uses audited FY2025: fair value $45.79 to $41.40 a share, composite 58.65 to 57.87 (C). The fallback is disclosed ("revenue present in only 3/4 latest quarters — TTM basis suppressed ...; latest annual statement used instead"). The gate is not changed here, because it serves every TTM consumer; per-field TTM net income and ROTE that survive a revenue quarter withheld for presentation are routed to B5.
- **House constants.**
  - `SYNONYM_FLOOR_TOLERANCE` = { relative: 0.005, absolute: 2,000,000 }: a non-negative candidate is below a positive component only when it is below it by more than the larger of 0.5% of the component and 2,000,000 in the row's currency. Revisit it if a census replay shows a floor that should have fired staying silent.
  - `RESTATEMENT_THRESHOLD_PCT` (1%), reused as the re-presentation threshold: for a re-filed minuend or subtrahend, for a filing that re-presented earlier periods and for a moved discontinued-operations line.
  - `ROUNDING_UNIT` (1,000,000) and `ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE` (500,000): a later money copy that is a whole multiple of a million and within half a million of the earlier copy only re-rounds it and is not a move (Task 7 review, I2), so such a re-filing keeps the as-filed pair.
  - The first-reported minuend stands in only when the subtrahend did not move with the minuend, the winner is not an amendment, and the re-filing moved it by at most 1% or labels the period a re-presentation (a non-zero `DISCONTINUED_LABEL_TAGS` fact for the period in the re-filing that is new there or moved by more than 1% from its first-reported copy); otherwise the quarter is withheld (C-9). The same threshold and label test is applied to every subtrahend of a kept pair against its newest copy filed after the minuend's filing (OD-5 (a2′)).
  - A presentation refusal ends the field: no later synonym, stand-in or derivation of any chain serves it (the plan said it ends its synonym step; the Task 7 review made it the whole field), except the M-6 subset skip above.
- **Versions.** Report 1.49.0, payload 1.51.0 and Stage B ACCOUNTING_EVIDENCE_30 mark these conventions; pipeline stage-c-1.6.13, the score bands and `FAIR_VALUE_METHOD_VERSION`, `SCENARIO_TARGET_METHOD_VERSION`, `SCENARIO_PATHS_METHOD_VERSION` and `NET_DEBT_RESOLVER_VERSION` are unchanged: no Stage C pass, band table, valuation method or resolver changed, only the filed inputs they read. `EDGAR_DERIVED_LINES_SINCE_SPEC_VERSION` is frozen at "1.49.0" and is never compared with `REPORT_SPEC_VERSION` itself. The DEMO delta group `b13-edgar-derived-lines-20261029` holds only the report stamp; the payload golden moves its version header and gains the FIN-509-V1 entry and its citation (+429 bytes).
- **Preservation.** Stored reports and snapshots keep their bytes (D-67). A report before spec 1.49.0 whose income statements were built from SEC filings, in full (an exact `keyless.incomeAnnual` or `keyless.incomeQuarterly` entry starting "served by edgar") or for older backfilled periods, is shown through `withLegacyEdgarDerivedLines` with fixed notes on its fair-value basis, its quality notes and, when an income restatements entry names revenue or ends "and N more", its quarterly trend; a provider-route report is returned unchanged (Task 10b).
- **Validation.**
  - `tests/edgar.derivedLines.audit20261027.test.ts`, `tests/edgar.presentationLineage.audit20261027.test.ts`, `tests/edgar.financialEnrichment.q4Basis.audit20261027.test.ts`, `tests/filingDisclosures.trendBasis.audit20261027.test.ts`, `tests/stageB.reitFfoTotalDa.audit20261027.test.ts`, `tests/stageB.forensics.oneTimeGap.audit20261027.test.ts` and `tests/report.legacyEdgarDerivedLines.test.ts`; each new test failed first, except the controls.
  - Replay of the 45 census snapshots and the stored provider runs, main `ca3726b` against the branch at `61b2841`, offline with no provider, SEC or model call: 625 census cells move, every one attributed to a task and a filed figure; no forensic flag moves; Task 8 moves no value. The only band moves are Eli Lilly's (business quality C to B, 69.79 to 70.91; balance sheet ungraded to C, 68.57), with its DCF $842.45 to $1,079.16. Other headline moves: J&J DCF $129.37 to $141.18 and EV/EBITDA 24.98x to 19.74x; BAC fair value $45.79 to $41.40; McDonald's FY2025 D&A 457M to 2,199M and net debt/EBITDA 3.352x to 2.952x; Cisco's FY2025 and FY2026 D&A withheld; JPMorgan's FY2025 interest income 28,032M to 193,341M; composites of J&J, Realty Income, ExxonMobil, Chevron and Cisco within 0.1 of their main values. The table is in the disposition record.
- **Limits.** The residual list in the disposition record names where each is routed: B5 (the BAC TTM, and FIN-402's possible second removal of a charge inside a subtracted "other" line), R1a Task 25 (income classification against a derived quarter), R1a Task 12 (`millionsPair` for R0's texts), R1 addendum 3 (the pre-existing keyless enrichment self-conflicts at McDonald's and Walmart), B4 (its XOM and JNJ baselines move with FIN-509), and the post-fix audit (verification plan Task V7) for the rest.

## D-135 - Audit 2026-10-27 batch B4a: the equity bridge, EV and invested capital count every claim once (2026-10-29)

Audit 2026-10-27, batch B4, part A (B4a): FIN-103, FIN-119, FIN-119-V1, FIN-119-V2, FIN-303, FIN-303-V1, FIN-108, FIN-304, FIN-305, FIN-305-V1, FIN-305-V2, FIN-403, FIN-404, FIN-109 and FIN-311, three of them High (FIN-119, FIN-303, FIN-305). Part B (B4b: convertibles, equity-method stakes, fair-value financial assets) is a separate batch with its own entry. The owner delegated the calls ("use your recommendation based on research to make this a professional accurate repository"); following the one-entry-per-batch practice, OD-1, OD-3, OD-4, OD-6, OD-7 and OD-8 are recorded here, one bullet each, with their full sources in the batch plan ([`docs/internal/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-audit-fix-04-equity-bridge-and-invested-capital.md`](https://github.com/eligorelick/Metis/blob/d4bf240068ff1faa3d57fe84a0359488602dd6d6/docs/internal/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-audit-fix-04-equity-bridge-and-invested-capital.md)) and the [disposition record](2026-10-27-audit-batch-b4-equity-bridge.md). The after-tax convention of OD-4 was decided by the main session on the owner's delegation (decisions spec, section 4.3). Every rule is class-wide; none names a ticker. The number D-135 is next after B13's D-134 and is renumbered at merge, with the stamps below, if another batch lands first.

- **OD-1: redeemable (temporary) equity is a claim senior to common.**
  - Decision: one house definition of claims senior to common: permanent preferred plus redeemable preferred (`TemporaryEquityCarryingAmountAttributableToParent`), and book NCI plus redeemable NCI (`RedeemableNoncontrollingInterestEquityCarryingAmount`). The DCF bridge deducts the redeemable preferred beside preferred; the redeemable NCI joins book NCI as the book floor of E-5's `max(book, profit share x consolidated equity value)`, so it is never deducted twice. The market EV, the own-history EV and the REIT EV add both. Invested capital (ROIC, sales-to-capital, the A-2 history) adds the admitted total, because the cash it raised is already netted. The claims reach every guard that asks whether preferred or NCI exists: forecast operating EPS, the P/FCF cash-ownership guard and the own-history common-allocation checks.
  - A null book NCI is never read as 0 plus the redeemable NCI (pre-flight I2): the per share stays withheld under E-5 and the reason names the redeemable NCI. A total with no parent/NCI split is deducted beside preferred, and withholds the per share when E-5's earnings-share basis would apply (`valuation.dcf.temporaryEquityAllocation`). An operand Stage A refuses (a conflict, a non-finite value) withholds what it touches, at warn severity, and is never zero-filled (D-87); a refused year is a non-debt refusal in ROIC's existing refusal list, so it never turns R0's WACC-balance critical rule on (I3).
  - In the P/FCF guard a redeemable NCI takes the book-NCI materiality floor (SNOW-2): it withholds unless the book NCI is known and the book and redeemable NCI together, and the NCI income, are each at most 1% of consolidated equity; a redeemable preferred, an unsplit amount or a refused operand withholds at any size. The replay found the missing floor withholding Tesla's P/FCF for a claim 0.004% of its market cap.
  - Residual: the parent part can also hold redeemable common stock (ESOP puts, SPAC Class A) that the diluted count already holds, which companyfacts cannot separate; the bridge note says so in the report itself.
  - Measured at main (I1): temporary equity is present for UNH, WMT, TSLA, T and CMCSA, and in history years for NEE, DIS and CVX.
  - Rejected: disclose only (it leaves a known, sourced claim inside common equity); deduct redeemable NCI outside E-5 (it double counts whenever the earnings key applies); zero-fill a refused allocation (D-87).
  - Revises: D-87's scope note (this entry is the admission basis it asked for); extends E-5 (D-102) with the redeemable floor.
  - Sources: Deloitte Roadmap, *Noncontrolling Interests* 9.4, and *SEC Comment Letter Considerations* 2.16 (redeemable equity "should not be included in any total or subtotal captioned 'total equity'"); Koller, Goedhart and Wessels, *Valuation*, 7th ed., ch. 16.
- **OD-3: one lease basis for invested capital.**
  - Decision: extend D-25 and D-97 item 3. On the default switch every invested-capital consumer (DCF sales-to-capital, the A-2 history row by row, ROIC) removes the operating-lease slice from total debt exactly when the bridge does: the slice is positive, at most total debt, and `operatingLeaseScopeUnproven` is null (the CODE-1 proof). One shared predicate, `operatingLeaseOutOfDebt`, replaces the per-consumer copies. With the lease-inclusive switch set every consumer keeps the slice; an unproven row keeps total debt as reported, and its note says the scope is unproven.
  - One lease basis per A-2 median: the history is measured on the current balance's basis, and a year whose scope is unproven cannot be put on the lease-excluded basis, so it is left out of the median with a note, never kept lease-inclusive beside lease-excluded years.
  - Lease-emptied capital (I6): when the lease leaves debt and invested capital is not positive, sales-to-capital takes the issuer's own history on the same basis (at least three usable years, `S2C_HISTORY_MIN_YEARS`, within the house cap); otherwise the DCF is withheld with a warn gap naming the invested capital and the lease basis (lead `LEASE_EMPTIED_CAPITAL_LEAD`; warn, not critical, because main published a DCF on the lease-inclusive capital and a critical gap would block the report; the fair value and scenario targets quote it). It never falls back to the mixed basis.
  - Rejected: a lease-inclusive sales-to-capital on purpose (it charges leased capacity twice); capitalising leases everywhere (D-25 option b).
  - Revises: nothing; it applies D-25 and D-97 item 3 to omitted consumers. It supersedes the batch-2b review row that treated leases as capital for the A-2 history without a D-entry (`docs/audit/2026-10-22-audit-batch2b-valuation-mediums.md`, left as history).
  - Sources: CBIZ, "What changes to the lease accounting standards means for business valuation" (ASC 842 expense stays above EBITDA; mixing the two bases diminishes value); D-25.
- **OD-4: debt-like obligations beyond E-7, all deducted after tax.**
  - Decision: pension and OPEB deficits, loss-contingency accruals and contingent consideration join E-7's reader and bridge lines. Read at the bridge date, else the latest filed balance within a year (no further back than an annual balance sheet that no longer tags it); a balance filed as zero ends the look-back. Pension takes the broadest recognised family at the date, never summed across families, in the order (a) `PensionAndOtherPostretirementAndPostemploymentBenefitPlansLiabilities`, (b) `PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilities`, (c) the defined-benefit pension plus the other postretirement liability; the look-back is date first (each date newest first, the families in order at each date). Overfunded plans are not credited, and postemployment benefits count only inside family (a). A current-only loss-contingency accrual or earn-out counts as the whole, and only the amount above any same-date environmental accrual is deducted for loss contingencies. None joins the market EV, and the EV basis says so.
  - Tax: all five families (asset-retirement, environmental, pension and OPEB, loss contingencies, contingent consideration) are deducted at `net x (1 - rate)`, with `rate` the D-98 marginal-rate floor the bridge already uses for its investment tax (21% for a US domicile, 15% elsewhere; no new rate). `net` is the amount E-7 deducted before (after a settlement-fund offset), so the relief never applies to the offset; each claim stays one netted line labelled "(filed, after tax at {rate}%...)". The closing note says the relief is approximate: state and local taxes are omitted, the deduction is assumed taken against taxable income when paid, and a payment that is not deductible (a government fine or penalty, 26 U.S.C. section 162(f)) or that only adds to tax basis (contingent consideration: the acquired assets' basis, amortised over 15 years for intangibles, or the acquired shares' basis, recovered only on a sale) is credited a relief it will not earn, or not for years. With no resolved rate the full amount is deducted and E-7's before-tax sentence is kept. This revises E-7's before-tax choice (D-104) and resolves known issue B2b-1; it was decided by the main session on the owner's delegation (decisions spec 4.3). For a pension deficit, `net x (1 - rate)` is the after-tax cost of funding it at once; the bridge does not model a slower schedule, which costs more in present value.
  - Rate-regulated utilities (I7): a filer whose SIC is 4911, 4923, 4924, 4931, 4932 or 4941 (the codes `src/edgar/sic.ts` maps to a regulated electric, gas or water utility or a diversified utility; the first ruling's range 4900-4991 was withdrawn because it caught waste haulers, pipelines and cogenerators) is read as a rate-regulated utility (ASC 980) and has its pension and OPEB deficit disclosed, not deducted (a filer under 4911 whose rates do not recover the deficit, such as a merchant generator, is overstated by it after tax, and the note says so), because the offsetting regulatory asset is reported only in dimensional XBRL, which companyfacts does not carry. An unknown SIC is read as not a utility, with an info gap raised only when a pension line is actually deducted. Loss contingencies and earn-outs are still deducted at a utility. Residual, routed to the free-data-source batch: net the deficit against the pension regulatory asset once dimensional XBRL is available.
  - Rejected: disclose only; before tax for all five (E-7's convention and this plan's first version: practitioner and academic sources measure a pension deficit net of tax); after tax for pension alone (two tax conventions in one bridge); the filer's own deferred-tax asset per obligation (not tagged consistently, batch 2b's reason); a separate positive "tax relief" line (the bridge surfaces read only a component's sign); crediting overfunded plans (a US employer reversion pays a 20% excise tax, 50% unless a replacement plan, IRC 4980); adding pension to the market EV (the own-history EV ranks would compare two definitions).
  - Revises: E-7 (D-104): scope from two tag families to five, the tax convention from before tax to after tax for all five, and "a current portion alone is not the obligation" for the loss-contingency and contingent-consideration families only; it also revises `docs/audit/2026-10-17-book-to-code-disposition.md` (pensions listed as future liquidity work only). D-104's text and `docs/audit/2026-10-22-audit-batch2b-valuation-mediums.md` are history and stay as written; this entry supersedes their before-tax sentences ("the deduction is before tax" and "(filed, before tax"), which remain only as the no-rate branch and as the legacy-report detector in `src/report/legacyBridgeMethod.ts`.
  - Sources, as the plan recorded them (checked 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-28; not re-fetched when this entry was written, since no network was available): ASU 2017-07 as applied in Hexion's FY2017 10-K (other components of net benefit cost are outside income from operations); ASC 715 funded-status presentation; FE Training, "Pensions and OPEBs" ("subtract the pension or OPEB deficit net of any tax liability") and "Debt Equivalents"; IB Interview Questions, "Pensions and off-balance-sheet hidden liabilities" (Pension Adjustment = Unfunded Pension x (1 - Tax Rate)); 26 U.S.C. section 404(a) (contributions are deductible), section 461(h)(2)(C) (a tort liability's economic performance occurs as payments are made) and section 162(f)(1); Porte Brown, "Tax issues when buying a business with an earnout"; Hectelion glossary, "Debt-like items"; Law Insider, "Debt-Like Items"; D-98 "Tax on investments". Feldstein, "Private Pensions as Corporate Debt", in *The Changing Roles of Debt and Equity in Financing U.S. Capital Formation* (NBER, 1982, pp. 75-90, chapter c11396), is cited for the net-of-tax principle by its citation only: its page images, read offline on 2026-10-28, were lost the same day, so it was not re-checked and nothing is quoted from it. The decision does not rest on it.
- **OD-6: a holding above invested capital is added back.**
  - Decision: a filed non-operating holding is added in the bridge at carrying value less the D-98 tax whether or not removing it leaves positive operating capital. When removing it leaves none, the operating ratio is unbounded and sales-to-capital takes the house cap `S2C_CLAMP[1]` (5.0), the limit the ratio approaches from below; the clamp note names the reason, and the A-2 history counts such a year at the cap. On the current-capital rule DCF equity value does not fall when investments rise; the A-2 history median's 0.1 cutoff predates this and can still step when the bridge row is also a history row.
  - Rejected: keeping the D-58 fallback (the holding valued at zero, a discontinuity of up to 4.8% a share for 1B more investments); withholding the DCF at the boundary.
  - Revises: the D-58 fallback in METHODOLOGY and the code note "When removing them would leave no operating capital the D-58 basis stands" (both rewritten); D-65 item 4 stays true and now also covers what sales-to-capital could not remove.
  - Sources: D-65's own principle ("an asset left out of operating capital is never left out of value too"); Damodaran, "Holdings in Other Firms".
- **OD-7: the divisor in a loss period.**
  - Decision: a loss row's filed diluted count equals basic, so the divisor is the loss row's basic count plus the newest award-dilution increment from a profitable period among the latest four quarters and the latest fiscal year (that period's diluted count less its basic count, less any filed conversion increment). The substitution is dated and disclosed (info gap `valuation.perShare.lossPeriodDivisor`) and reaches the DCF, excess-return and REIT per share and forecast EPS. (Revised by D-233: the REIT per share divides by the latest fiscal year's count, so the substitution reaches it when that fiscal year is the loss period, not when the latest quarter is.) With no profitable donor, the basic count stands and the D-60 note and METHODOLOGY say it carries no option or RSU dilution. Detection (`dilutedDivisor.ts`): both counts are positive, the diluted count is at most basic plus 1 (`diluted <= basic + 1`), and the row's income from continuing operations (net income when that is not filed) is below zero. The conversion subtraction: the donor's filed if-converted share increment (debt and preferred) is taken out of its increment, because the bridge deducts those claims. The not-restored case: when the issuer has a convertible instrument filed with a nonzero balance (in any reporting currency) within 366 days and the donor period files no conversion increment, the award increment could hold conversion shares, so it is not restored, the filed count divides, and an info note says so (`loss-period-withheld`).
  - Rejected: the newest profitable period's diluted count (it carries that period's older basic count); disclose only.
  - Revises: D-65 item 5 and the D-60 divisor disclosure; METHODOLOGY "Share basis".
  - Sources: Deloitte Roadmap, *Earnings per Share* 8.7 (with a loss from continuing operations, diluted EPS is computed as basic EPS); ASC 260-10-45-17 to 45-20.
- **OD-8: one REIT market cap and EV.**
  - Decision: the REIT block takes its market cap and its EV from the multiples framework: the quote's admitted market cap and the house EV, which after OD-1 holds preferred, redeemable preferred, book NCI and redeemable NCI. P/FFO and P/AFFO are market cap over FFO at both sites; FFO and AFFO per share stay on the diluted count. (Revised by D-233: the diluted count of FFO's own fiscal year, not the latest quarter's.) A quote with a price but no market cap withholds P/FFO and EV with a warn gap. OP units, permanent or redeemable, are not common shares, so adding them as NCI never double counts.
  - Rejected: price times weighted diluted shares (two P/FFOs and two EVs per report, and OP units counted twice once redeemable NCI joins the EV); moving the multiples to price over FFO per diluted share (it touches peer and own-history P/FFO, not in this batch).
  - Revises: D-26's sentence "the REIT implied cap rate uses the house enterprise value", made true by construction instead of by a parallel formula.
  - Sources: Deloitte Roadmap 9.4 (that OP units redeemable for cash are such an NCI is filer practice, not the roadmap's); METHODOLOGY ("a report carries one EV").
- **FIN-403: a successor reads its predecessor's retirement obligations.** A holding-company successor whose own companyfacts carry no retirement obligation reads the predecessor's, as one reporting entity under B-36, until the successor's own annual report; a family the successor files, including a zero, ends the predecessor read for that family, and a family both file is read once, from the successor. Extends E-7 and B-36.
- **FIN-103: the DCF bridge reads the statement-date balance.** When an annual base is rolled forward, D-65's promise that the bridge stays at the statement-date balance is now checked: the bridge row follows the DCF's basis with one refusal rule (a newer quarter with no debt line falls back to the older complete balance), and the bridge note and an info gap `valuation.dcf.bridgeBalanceDate` name the date used. The refusal rule is the one the DCF reads on the row: a parser refusal, unresolved ownership, a lease conflict, a lease-scope refusal (on the run's own lease switch) or a refused temporary-equity operand. (Revised by D-248: "unresolved ownership" is now the P5 owner's one predicate and allowance, `noncontrollingOwnershipUnresolved` in `src/pipeline/stageB/ownership.ts`; the row choice no longer keeps a copy with its own one-part-in-a-billion allowance, so a gap of under one currency unit between consolidated and parent equity no longer refuses a row and a whole-unit gap now does.) The first clean candidate at the statement date is the row; when every candidate is refused, or the anchor is, the anchor (main's row) stands, never cured by another date, so no report main publishes is blocked by the choice (final review I-2).
- **Final whole-branch review (fix round 1), the merge rule: no report main publishes becomes Blocked, and no figure is worse than main.** (I-1) Lease-emptied invested capital withholds the DCF at warn (OD-3). (M-1) A row with a refused temporary-equity operand and a lease conflict or lease-scope refusal keeps main's critical lease gap beside the warn. (M-7) A null book NCI beside a redeemable NCI takes the P/FCF 1% floor on the redeemable NCI alone; with no redeemable NCI the guard is main's. (M-9) A positive `preferredStock` equal to the admitted redeemable preferred within max(1, 1e-6 x amount) at the same date (the filer tagged one mezzanine series `PreferredStockValue` and `TemporaryEquityCarryingAmountAttributableToParent`) is counted once: `temporaryEquityClaims`, the one reader, leaves the parent part out and the preferred line main already deducts stands, so no balance row is altered; an info gap `valuation.preferredOverlap` names both tags once per date; unequal amounts are both deducted (B4b's overlap territory, OD-2). (M-8) The rate-regulated note states the reading, not rate recovery.
- **House constants.**
  - The pension family order (a), (b), (c) and its date-first look-back.
  - The six SIC codes read as rate-regulated: 4911, 4923, 4924, 4931, 4932, 4941.
  - The house cap `S2C_CLAMP[1]` (5.0) taken when operating capital is not positive (FIN-304).
  - The three-year minimum reused for lease-emptied capital (`S2C_HISTORY_MIN_YEARS`; no new constant).
  - D-98's marginal-rate floor reused as the debt-like lines' tax rate (no new rate).
  - The 1% share of consolidated equity (`IMMATERIAL_NCI_SHARE_OF_EQUITY`) reused as the redeemable-NCI floor in the P/FCF guard.
- **Versions.** Report 1.50.0, payload 1.52.0, Stage B `STAGE_B_2026_10_ACCOUNTING_EVIDENCE_31`, `FAIR_VALUE_2026_10_D135` and `SCENARIO_TARGETS_2026_10_D135`, each next after the preceding merge; pipeline stage-c-1.6.13 and the score bands are unchanged. `BRIDGE_METHOD_SINCE_SPEC_VERSION` is frozen at "1.50.0" and is never compared with `REPORT_SPEC_VERSION` itself. Stored reports keep their bytes (D-67); a report before 1.50.0 shows a fixed method note on its DCF, excess-return and REIT values through `withLegacyBridgeMethod`.
- **Validation.** Each finding's test failed first. The replay of the 45 census snapshots and the stored provider runs (main `55dc846` against the branch, offline, no provider, SEC or model call) attributes every moved figure to a task and a filed amount, and no composite band moves. The table, XOM line by line and the band moves are in the [disposition record](2026-10-27-audit-batch-b4-equity-bridge.md), which also lists the residuals (WACC weights and temporary equity, the approximation of the tax relief, the utility pension netting, redeemable common stock in parent temporary equity, and the rest).

## D-136 - Audit B5a (2026-10-27): seasonality, 52/53-week calendars and the guided quarter on one basis

PR review clarification (2026-10-30): without a filed start, a quarterly length is inferred only when the predecessor's end is adjacent under the existing 70–135-day quarter rule. Missing earlier quarters leave duration unknown; an otherwise complete latest TTM is retained. Annual fallback separately uses the previous annual end. This fixes the erroneous 182-day quarter and synthetic 100% growth in PR #77's gap case, without changing the annual convention.

Recorded after the E1/E5 replay and threshold gates passed. D-136 and the versions below are next after the fetched B4a main (`222f92a`); recheck numbering before merge. This entry covers Part A of the [B5 plan](https://github.com/eligorelick/Metis/blob/d4bf240068ff1faa3d57fe84a0359488602dd6d6/docs/internal/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-audit-fix-05-seasonality-calendars-and-dcf-inputs.md). Part B's terminal-return, transition-period, WACC, margin, tax and reverse-DCF changes are not implemented here.

- **OD-1: one period basis.** Revise D-58's run-rate and guidance level, D-60 choice 3's guidance-consistency floor, and D-98's sequential fallback. An exact whole-week quarter is scaled by 13/w before annualisation or a year-over-year comparison; 90-92-day calendar quarters stay unchanged. Non-whole-week lengths stay unscaled. An unknown length is read as 13 weeks and disclosed. A 371-day DCF starting period is scaled by 52/53, including its operating flows and tagged one-off. Ratios use the filed operands because that common factor cancels: this preserves the exact existing margin, tax, capital-efficiency and scenario-shock calculations, including floating-point precision. Filed historical statements are unchanged.
- **R1's guidance level and floor.** For the same fiscal quarter a year earlier, let q be its 13-week revenue, T its four-quarter total, P the preceding four-quarter total, and rho = (T/P)^0.25. Its growth-adjusted seasonal factor is (q/T) / [rho^3/(1 + rho + rho^2 + rho^3)]. Average up to three such yearly factors. Divide the guided midpoint, on a 13-week basis, by that mean, multiply by four, then carry it 4.5 months at the guided year-over-year rate. With fewer than eight usable quarters ending at the year-ago quarter, year one is TTM times (1 + guided YoY). Without a usable year-ago comparison, keep the existing run-rate/TTM anchor and disclose why; a sequential change never substitutes for YoY. The consistency floor is the 13-week guided low plus the other three quarters of the starting base, held at their year-ago level for growth or reduced at the guided low's YoY pace for contraction. A known weekday calendar establishes Q4's end and length; other guided quarters on it stay weekly even when the preceding end coincides with month end. A future quarter whose extra-week placement is unknown says it assumes 13 weeks.
- **Rejected alternatives, with pre-flight provenance.** The first-planned TTM-times-guided-growth rule is retained only as the short-history fallback. At B13 it raised guidance-led NVDA from 434.00 to 515.94 a share (+18.88%), putting year one 9.0% above consensus versus main's 4.3%; it raised census AMZN by 5.25% and AMZN #43 by 3.75%. Dividing by a share of the fiscal year instead read NVDA's rapid growth as a 31.5% seasonal peak. Those are the pre-flight counterfactuals, not this branch's before/after values. The binding R1 rule averages up to three factors; the pre-flight's illustrative amended values measured only one. The implementation follows the formula, with a three-factor regression and no calibration to those illustrations.
- **R2 and R4: comparable growth, with the issuer's caveats.** The reverse-DCF context publishes the guided quarter's YoY pace beside the existing base-case, consensus and latest-quarter YoY rows. It drops the guidance-times-four and sequential context rows. A next-quarter guide does not set a twelve-month thesis trigger. Raw outlook qualifiers travel from their own release to the guided row; qualifiers from the release matching the latest quarter's end travel to that row. A stated "excluding ... year-over-year growth would be ... basis points higher/lower" effect is recorded in signed percentage points and disclosed, without changing guidance. Calendar-shifted events, FX and divestitures need a timing-versus-persistent classifier before an ex-event level is justified. The pre-flight's AMZN option was 869.44B / 105.95 a share (+7.22% against B13 main, within 0.8% of keyed consensus 876.36B); it remains an unimplemented later-batch option.
- **OD-1a: future fiscal-year ends.** Infer exactly one last-weekday or nearest-weekday-to-month-end rule from at least three newest annual ends chained 364 or 371 days apart. Snap an estimate date only when exactly one implied year end is within ten days. When an admitted estimate has no preceding contiguous estimate, derive its start from the rule's preceding year end, including a December rule ending in January; a 53-week year must not retain a 365-day anniversary denominator when YTD is unavailable. Existing contiguous-estimate chaining and the fallback for an unadmitted date remain unchanged. Ambiguity, an interrupted chain or a calendar change keeps the vendor date and discloses an approximate boundary when appropriate. This is a house inference from filed dates, not a ticker table. D-99 finding 19's forecast windows are unchanged.
- **Scope extension E1.** Confirmed by the main session (decisions spec 4.3, 2026-10-28) on its replay evidence: extend the same 13-week basis to D-65's interest run-rate. The current exact base/Task 1 replay has 26 calls over 52 inputs. Only census PEP's 84-day quarter ending 2026-09-05 moves: 941,390,093.2564788 to 1,019,839,267.6945186, exactly 13/12 within 1e-9 relative. COST's 112-day and MU #46's 98-day latest quarters close their fiscal years, so neither calls the quarter-interest path; KO's 93-day quarter is not a whole number of weeks and stays unchanged.
- **Census evidence E5.** On Task 2 (`21265df`) against Task 3 (`2ab443d`), all 50 census/keyed inputs plus AMZN #51/#52 were compared with their saved configuration. Only guidance-led census NVDA, census AMZN and AMZN #43 change year one or DCF value. NVDA's mean factor is 1.09964342303034, from 1.0193048814079904, 0.9050296941259413 and 1.3745956935570887; year one is 548.968521B -> 499.224121B and value 424.380063 -> 297.517973 (-29.8935%). This is the named over-10% move: the required three-factor mean differs materially from the illustrative single factor. Against each side's correctly dated keyed comparison, the year-one gap shrinks from +4.29% to -3.31%, and the per-share gap also shrinks. AMZN's mean 0.9934009499710115 gives 829.089573B -> 834.597121B; census value 101.811471 -> 102.974150 and #43 value 86.377176 -> 87.172750. Consensus-led inputs do not move in this commit pair. Older growth-regime changes can still be read as season; that residual is disclosed, not fitted away.
- **House-threshold backtest.** No network call or threshold retuning. Across 45 keyless census issuers, nine have an unambiguous weekday rule; the rule misclassifies none of the 45 census issuers. Withhold each of 131 eligible year ends and fit both the nearest three and all older chained ends: 231 exact predictions, 31 no-rule results, zero wrong. The 462 anniversary/month-end snap trials have distances 0-6 days (counts 36, 208, 91, 40, 11, 32, 44 respectively); every competing year end is 359-367 days away. The week-count by-product admits non-13-week scaling only for exact whole weeks, with 90-92 days left at 13; 1,174 known quarter lengths across the census and five keyed inputs range 84-119 days. The 1,029 admitted four-quarter windows span 252-287 days, all inside the 250-300-day year-ago position; one NNN window retains the existing gap refusal. The disposition table records the complete distributions, non-whole-week cases and unknown lengths. The stub threshold and 0.75-year span belong to B5b.
- **Sources and limits.** The approved plan's sources are [Forecasting: Principles and Practice, seasonal naive forecasting](https://otexts.com/fpp3/simple-methods.html), [IAS 34's interim-reporting overview](https://www.iasplus.com/standard/ias34.htm), [Home Depot's FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/354950/000162828026019436/hd-20260201.htm), and [Silicon Graphics' disclosure that an extra week can occur in Q1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001316625/000131662513000021/a10q2013q3.htm). The weekday alternatives follow [26 CFR 1.441-2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.441-2), with quarterly-calendar context in [Chart House's filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000820757/000095013101500098/dex13.txt). These references are carried from the pre-flight; the averaging formula, ten-day tolerance and minimum history are house choices tested above. The looser seasonal floor can admit stale consensus; the existing bounded run-rate can understate a seasonal trough. Neither is silently retuned here.
- **Versions and stored reports.** Report 1.51.0, payload 1.53.0 and Stage B `STAGE_B_2026_10_ACCOUNTING_EVIDENCE_32` are next after B4a; `ANNUALIZATION_CONVENTION_SPEC` is frozen at "1.51.0". ## D-138 - Receivables concept continuity for forensic comparisons (2026-10-30, unreleased)

Task 3 of the [report-53 audit plan](https://github.com/eligorelick/Metis/blob/d4bf240068ff1faa3d57fe84a0359488602dd6d6/docs/internal/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-qcom-report-53-audit.md), governed by its [receivables contract](../internal/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-qcom-report-53-audit-design.md). This opening entry records the receivables change; subsequent additions record implemented tasks. Final release acceptance remains separate.

- **Decision.** DSRI and the receivables-versus-revenue growth flag consume one pair resolved after existing annual alignment and continuity checks. Preserve an admitted same-concept pair. Unknown vendor scope keeps the same numbers, adverse flag presence/severity and thresholds, with a visible unverified-scope qualification instead of a company-specific channel-stuffing explanation. The combined report carries the shared qualifier once; both standalone consumers retain it.
- **Uncertainty versus contradiction.** Missing metadata and unsupported multi-tag/derived/calculated shapes alone remain unverified and preserve existing numerical behavior. Explicit matching field units can supply a missing duplicate row currency label. Explicit incompatible units/issuer identities/endpoints, duration-versus-instant evidence, field conflicts or directly selected different concepts require repair or local refusal. QName equality establishes concept continuity, not a guessed trade-versus-total label.
- **Primary repair.** Replace both forensic observations together only from already acquired, issuer-confirmed facts. Require exact selected balance endpoints, established matching currency/issuer, direct instant/core-form facts, actual acquisition metadata, cutoff eligibility and a common filing presenting both endpoints. Retain copies so ambiguous or superseding contradictory/negative evidence cannot be ignored. Prefer the current selected concept, then existing tag order, never the favorable score. Without a complete repair use the existing disclosed DSRI neutralization and suppress its unsupported growth comparison. No new critical gap or Blocked state is introduced.
- **Preservation and rejected alternatives.** Raw statements, stored snapshots, revenue selection, capital/valuation inputs, inventory flags, coefficients, floors, clamps and thresholds are unchanged. Do not repair unknown vendor scope merely because filed alternatives exist, infer scope from matching values, remap a fiscal endpoint by one day, invent USD/acquisition time, reorder global synonyms or suppress genuinely adverse comparable evidence. The upstream statement-currency gate is unchanged.
- **Evidence and limits.** Synthetic controls use supplied total receivables 4,315M/3,929M and trade receivables 2,855M/2,347M, on revenue 44,284M/38,962M. They do not claim the retained report's exact QName/provider path: that snapshot is unavailable. A genuinely adverse 200M/100M pair on 1,100M/1,000M revenue keeps DSRI 1.81818 and both warnings, including when supplied through an admitted filed repair. Public-function RED, extraction/selection/integration controls, deep-freeze preservation and permutation tests support the change.
- **Final-review display correction.** The controlled repair note displays only a complete canonical hyphenated accession (10/2/6 digits), with fixed unavailable-for-display wording otherwise. Raw accession strings remain in evidence and the common-filing identity comparison; admission, selected pair, arithmetic, grades and state do not change. Real extractor-to-forensics-to-prompt tests reproduce malicious text outside source envelopes before the correction and exclude it afterward, with canonical and raw-evidence preservation controls. This is within the same unpublished D-138 stamps, not an original report-53 reconstruction.
- **Release boundary.** This is an unreleased, incremental decision. Any exact audit-delta group update requires dry attribution first. Later additions record the reserved stamps, payload restoration and saved-reader behavior. Final batch replay and release acceptance remain separate; none is claimed complete by this opening entry.

### D-138 Task 5 addition - bounded quarterly guidance tables (2026-10-30, unreleased)

- **Decision.** Future bounded extraction accepts one explicit current-only fiscal-quarter column using the parsed source document's actual two-cell rows. Revenue retains explicit endpoint scales and currency; diluted EPS retains separate GAAP/non-GAAP bases and exact per-share endpoints. Each observation retains its row and header coordinates in the same flattened source document. Controlled metric/period labels are generated from validated fields; raw header/row/issuer/date/currency strings do not become trusted model notes.
- **Refusals and preservation.** Duplicate/conflicting columns, metrics or guidance tables, merged cells, unsupported scope headings/captions, crossed source rows, mismatched endpoint scales/currencies and reversed ranges are not admitted. Unsupported row groups end the supported consolidated run. A recognized structural refusal prevents flattened-text rescue. The supported compact parser and release-before-commentary priority remain intact. No issuer-specific production values, extra fetch, new fiscal-calendar rule, model coefficient, grade/state rule or report-wide unknown-evidence refusal is introduced. Existing statement-currency, scale, B5 weekday-calendar and guide-retirement rules are reused unchanged.
- **Task 5 review correction.** Consolidated scope is positive proof, not the absence of a disallowed HTML heading. The new route requires a complete immediate supported label in a heading, paragraph or div within the 1,500-character markup window. Inline emphasis is allowed inside the proven label; an intervening paragraph/div/bold/strong label or other visible text invalidates the earlier scope. Missing/truncated context is refused locally and non-null, preventing prose rescue. The label must also occur at its flattened-source coordinate; script/style-only labels, including wrappers beginning outside the lookback, cannot establish visible scope. Generic controls preserve the exact primary values/bases/source spans and existing B5/compact behavior without a segment-name list.
- **Task 5 explicit-hidden correction.** Flattened coordinate agreement establishes source consistency, not general visibility. A local quote-aware fence declines the new structured-table route if any actual HTML `hidden` attribute remains anywhere in the preprocessed source, including boolean false-valued forms and ancestor openings outside the positive-scope window. Inspection is capped at 2,000,000 source characters; larger sources are refused by this route. Deliberately, even an unrelated closed hidden element declines the new layout. Ordinary quoted values and attribute lookalikes such as `data-hidden` do not trigger the fence; comment/script/style literals do not count as attributes. This is a conservative supported-layout limitation, not an all-CSS/browser visibility claim. The positive-scope window stays 1,500 characters and refusal stays non-null without prose rescue. Shared extraction, the independently approved event parser, legacy compact plain/HTML parsing, primary source spans/bases/values and all financial/stamp policies are unchanged.
- **Task 5 lexical ordering correction.** The negative fence now uses a bounded pure lexical helper that recognizes complete quoted tags and actual attribute names/values before interpreting genuine comments or script/style raw-text bodies. It does not destructively pre-remove delimiter-like attribute values. A real hidden attribute between quoted comment/script/style delimiters therefore remains a refusal, while spaced unquoted values such as `title = hidden` remain supported. Oversized, unterminated or unsupported lexical states conservatively decline the new structured route; this is not DOM repair or general CSS/browser visibility proof. Only the guidance caller adopts the helper here; shared extraction, Task 6 caller code and financial/version policies remain untouched. The whole-document negative fence, legacy exemption, 2M cap, source coordinates and non-null/no-prose-rescue boundary remain in place.
- **Evidence and limits.** The inline raw HTML control models source-derived Q4 FY26 Estimates structure and filed revenue 9.7B–10.5B, GAAP diluted EPS 1.22–1.42 and non-GAAP diluted EPS 2.05–2.25 from [the identified release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/804328/000080432826000085/qcom062826erex991.htm). Its markup and IDs are synthetic; it is not the exact retained QCOM HTML and no live fetch or historical report-53 replay is claimed. Document parsing, release construction, offline collection, filing disclosure, payload and DCF-admission controls retain the three distinct midpoints 10.1B/1.32/2.15, source identity, basis and precise spans. A renamed issuer parses generically. An ended Q4 remains forward while Q3 is latest and retires after Q4 is reported. Supplied annual consensus implies Q4 10.202B inside the corridor and retains consensus as anchor instead of forcing the filed midpoint.
- **Release boundary.** This addition changes future extraction only. Stored reports are not reparsed at read time and unknown historical collection coverage stays qualified. The already reserved report `1.53.0`, payload `1.55.0` and Stage B 34 stamps remain unchanged; earlier golden/cutoff contracts remain exact. Independent Task 5 review and Task 9's final whole-batch verification remain separate gates.

Do not invent a bottom-up beta from the existing peer collection: it contains no peer return histories/common regression window or validated unlever/relever basis. ### D-149: Lender review conventions (F1, F2, F12)

Owner delegated to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. For evidenced held-for-sale lenders, industrial EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales, net debt, net debt/EBITDA, interest coverage, gross margin, ROIC and ROIC-vs-WACC are not applicable. Warehouse and loan-owner funding is operating inventory finance; industrial leverage/coverage cannot measure solvency. Capital adequacy is not modelled, and the Balance Sheet aspect is not modelled. filed real assets and keep common grading: 46.50 D / 50.28 D. Full census O,

against both 66c9ea1e and ac4916f8, including integration effects.

### D-150: FIN-510-V1: ambiguous deferred-revenue siblings (2026-11-02)

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. Adopted:
withhold deferred revenue when `ContractWithCustomerLiabilityCurrent` and
`DeferredRevenueCurrent` disagree for the period, with a gap naming both tags
and amounts. Neither first-hit order nor a larger number establishes the
correct scope. This resolves the deferred-revenue residual in D-134 OD-4;
JNJ R&D and JPM operating interest income remain controls. A single sibling
or equal siblings remain available. HD FY2025 changes 1.500B -> withheld
(the other sibling is 2.575B); no score/FCF/valuation consumer changes.
The same evidence rule also withholds conflicting DIS periods and older
AAPL, META and ORCL rows, listed in the disposition. Stored reports and saved
input snapshots are immutable; re-admission of retained facts uses the new
rule without rewriting them.

### D-150: Cash-capex convention retained (2026-11-02)

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. Confirmed:
standardized FCF retains the statement/vendor cash-capex field, with the
existing disclosure that the basis can mix PP&E and software across quarters.
No calculation change. A PP&E-only or PP&E-plus-software convention would
change the basis for every issuer's FCF, P/FCF and DCF seed and requires a
separate complete remeasurement. The measured FIG difference is 1.302M on
231.012M FCF (0.6% rounded). Preserving the disclosed retained basis avoids
silently substituting an accounting convention without comparable period
inputs. METHODOLOGY states this plainly; no stored report is rewritten.
(Revised by D-239: a provider figure of exactly 0 is no longer retained as

## D-151 - N3: SEC-built rows on a filed-total conflict (2026-11-02)

### D-151: IPO conversion is not dilution

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. A rising
annual weighted-share trend spanning filed conversion facts, or a filed IPO
with a same-filing two-class participating-security allocation, is withheld
with its filing and reason. The counts remain visible. The reason is that a
change in the common EPS denominator does not prove economic dilution. This
uses issuer-admitted facts available by the run cutoff, never a ticker rule;
ordinary issuance and IPO-only evidence leave genuine dilution measurable.

### D-151: XBRL conflict labels

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. A retained
revenue classification conflict records a completed comparison, even when a
downstream validation cannot compare the refused value. Headers and exports
say conflict found and vendor revenue refused or replaced. The reason is to
describe what XBRL actually established instead of calling it skipped. Stored
metadata and report bytes remain unchanged; the label reads retained evidence.

### D-151: Revenue multiple eligibility

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. An open
annual vendor/filed revenue-definition conflict withholds EV/Sales, its own
history rank and peer comparison. An explicit row refusal has the same effect
as a failed validation check. A whole reconciled SEC row may restore
eligibility. The reason is to prevent a multiple using revenue the app itself
has refused, including a still-populated quarterly denominator.

### D-151: Whole filed income rows

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. In auto
mode a directly filed revenue-total conflict replaces the whole vendor row
only when the SEC operating statement reconciles on matching scope. This
recovers usable filed revenue without combining incompatible revenue and cost
bases. Bank routing remains authoritative; failed reconciliation retains refusal.

### D-151: Quarterly CFO rows

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. A vendor
quarterly CFO conflict uses the whole canonical SEC-derived quarter when its
filing lineage is established. This restores cash-flow consumers without
combining a filed CFO with vendor capex or other fields. Mixed TTM row sources
are disclosed and existing TTM gates remain binding.
Either conflicting vendor CFO alias qualifies. Existing derived-operand
rounding stays binding. Missing SEC cash-capex is an explicit replacement-row
investment-scope refusal, so the existing runway gate cannot extrapolate an
older vendor quarter over the missing recent-quarter operand.

### D-151: EPS follows the income row

The owner delegated this decision to the coordinator on 2026-11-01. Switched
income rows carry their own filed EPS and shares. Missing or refused SEC EPS
cannot fall back to vendor EPS. This prevents a contradicted quarterly EPS
from entering TTM P/E; P0's independent vendor EPS conflict guard remains.

Signed accrual display bands, conditional disclaimer, EPS currency admission, excess-return continuing value and all filing/issuer-website egress are described as implemented. ## D-153 - P2: DCF inputs and seasonality, with N1 (2026-11-02)

### D-153: Consistent DCF operating income (2026-11-02)

FIN-402, FIN-402-V1, FIN-402-V2 and FIN-502 follow B5 OD-7/OD-12: use admitted
one-offs consistently in coverage, terminal evidence, margin history/ceiling
and the bounded tax reread. Historical families recurring in at least three of
five years remain costs. Reported ROIC remains GAAP. Unknown deductibility is
bounded rather than guessed. Stored reports are immutable; proven mismatched
tax seeds receive a display note below the frozen 1.56.0 cutoff.

### D-153: Retain terminal operating losses (2026-11-02)

FIN-102 implements B5 OD-2, revising D-99 only for FCFF terminal evidence:
a known operating loss counts against the every-year hurdle at zero tax.
Reported ROIC, moat grades and excess-return financial routes retain their
conventions. A normalized profitable year remains profitable evidence.

### D-153: Transition annual flows (2026-11-02)

FIN-111 takes B5 OD-3/O-2's conditional 357-day line. The offline gate found
434 filed-start income years, two gap-measured income years, 393 cash-flow
periods and 779 deduplicated annual companyfacts periods, all 364-371 days.
No full year was withheld. The oldest unknown-duration row stays; margins
remain displayed. Transition flows leave annual growth and valuation history.
The census has no transition filing, so periods of 357 days or more remain an
explicit residual. No threshold was retuned.

### D-153: Reverse DCF families and domain (2026-11-02)

FIN-501 follows OD-11: terminal-margin candidates preserve the base fade shape;
flat paths use a linear ramp. FIN-104 extends the existing DCF domain to every
reverse candidate, bracket and bound (FIN-104). A domain break withholds the
outside-range inference rather than implying a price-supported growth rate.

### D-153: FIN-116 (2026-11-02)

The latest debt balance used for WACC weights also admits the debt leg. Average debt is only the effective-rate denominator; newly borrowed debt cannot imply an all-equity rate, and fully repaid debt needs no debt cost. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-405 (2026-11-02)

Latest revenue YoY and acceleration are withheld when their endpoint is older than the newest annual flow row; an older comparison cannot be dated as current in the payload or report. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-127 (2026-11-02)

Historical projection rows carry the filed fiscalYear, including start-year retailer labels. When labels collide, both actuals receive distinct ended-date labels across revenue, operating margin, FCF and EPS; no actual is collapsed. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-114 (2026-11-02)

The WACC and DCF assumption source labels name the selected domicile ERP country. US is reserved for the US row or US fallback; country selection and numerical ERP are unchanged. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-113 (2026-11-02)

Current-capital windows use the established oldest-quarter start, including 52/53-week windows. Without an established start the calendar-anniversary fallback is explicitly approximate in the AI context. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-115 (2026-11-02)

Discount-rate notes and manifest gaps name the debt cost actually accepted. A rejected historical rate is labelled rejected; synthetic-use wording appears only after a synthetic rate is computable, and unavailable outcomes say so. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-118 (2026-11-02)

Headline valuation degradation excludes market-cap history and enterprise-value history. Daily and SPY price substitutions are named only when the selected WACC beta consumes the keyless regression; the provider-fallback manifest still retains every substitution. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-406 (2026-11-02)

A vendor effective tax ratio cannot create a WACC shield when the same statement window establishes non-positive pre-tax income. The existing zero-shield basis applies equally to keyed and keyless runs, including positive net income from below-line gains. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: FIN-512 (2026-11-02)

Scenario shocks retain their existing 25pp growth and 12pp margin bounds. Binding caps disclose the uncapped sample sigma beside the bounded shock in target and projection bases; optional raw fields retain compatibility, and judge framing names the bounds. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: RPT-502 (2026-11-02)

Available-scenario assumptions now state that runs outside the DCF domain are withheld. The obsolete negative-equity floor-at-zero claim is removed; deterministic scenario targets and stored report bytes remain unchanged. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: N1 (2026-11-02)

When one trailing quarter has positive SBC at least 3x the median of the other positive quarters, disclose its date and amount and the comparison median beside after-SBC FCF uses. Publish an other-three-quarter sum x 4/3 run-rate companion. House-default cash flow and scoring stay unchanged. No IPO or other cause is inferred without dated filed evidence. Stored reports remain immutable.

### D-153: Stored input-convention display (2026-11-02)

FIN-102/104/113/116/118 and RPT-502 apply the frozen 1.56.0 display cutoff.
Only established stored evidence permits a correction or qualification. Old
terminal years, debt-leg and range claims receive notes. Current-capital
metadata can take an unambiguous filed start; commentary text with verification
marks stays recorded. Degradation labels follow actual stored dependencies;
the exact obsolete scenario-method sentence takes the domain convention.
All source bytes and numeric figures remain immutable. The 51-report replay
also covers missing early score arrays and repeated view application.

### D-153: FIN-102 capital refusal boundary (2026-11-02)

The B5b Task 6 controller ruling preserves B4a refusals: an operating-loss year
with unknown or nonpositive invested capital remains missing. The loss flag
is attached only after a positive denominator is admitted. The terminal rule
requires an established numeric return and never substitutes zero for it.

### D-153: Full-year recurrence window (2026-11-02)

FIN-111's transition admission also applies to FIN-402-V2's three-of-five
recurrence window. A stub cannot displace the oldest full fiscal year and
turn a recurring tagged cost into an add-back. Coverage retains its own-window
normalization convention. The five-year terminal/margin evidence reads the

## D-154 - N4a: FIGR issuer capitalization, aggregate P/E, lender peers and gaps (2026-11-02)

### D-154: Cover counts and same-filing class rights (L1)

Admit dated primary-cover class observations only when the member set maps

Keep the ownership gate. The failure was the missing Q1 common-income field in

FY-minus-nine-month numerator already existed. Supplement only an absent,
non-refused common field with exact issuer/period/currency/cutoff proof through

Exclude candidates whose profile-only screen cannot confirm the SEC evidence
that establishes the subject's held-for-sale lending cash-flow applicability.

For an SEC-evidenced non-bank lender without an applicable FCFF or excess-return
