## D-182 - Findings from the first paid test (Haiku, META, 2026-11-03)

The owner allowed up to $25 of paid testing, tiered from cheaper to better models
so that each tier's findings are fixed before the next. Tier 1 ran META with
Haiku 4.5 analysts at medium effort (the judge is raised to the Sonnet 5.5 floor)
on merged main `b5fab23d`. The complete run cost $1.62. All passes completed and
verification was 100%. The one-hour synthesis cache was hit: judge sections 2 and
3 each read 169,077 cached tokens.

- **A month-only claim date cost a repair round.** The bull's first written case
  dated three claims "2026-01", "2026-07" and "2026-03" and failed the parse
  ($0.05 to repair on Haiku; the same failure would cost far more on Opus). A
  valid year-month or year is a coarser date, not a wrong one: it is now read as
  no date, as a blank already was. The claim's text keeps the period, and no day
  is invented, because a month-end day could read as a future date. Impossible
  values ("2026-13") and other malformed dates still fail.
- **The new sections were thin.** The judge listed 2 recent developments and 2
  management actions for a heavily covered company. The Q4 guidance it quoted in
  the executive summary was not listed as a management action. The rules now ask
  for each material dated development (typically 3-8 for a widely covered
  company) and each dated management action. Guidance issued with results,
  financings, buybacks, dividends and leadership changes each count. Both rules
  forbid padding with minor, routine or undated items.
- **Market structure was empty.** The judge read "use [] when no evidence
  supports a claim" as a reason to write nothing, because no source stated a
  market size, although the 10-K describes the competition. The rule now says to
  state once that no market size is sourced and still describe the industry
  structure and the company's position from the filing and the cases. [] is used
  only when neither discusses the industry.
- **A cost cap that cannot fit a run spends money for nothing.** A first attempt
  under a $3 job cap ran the bull ($0.44), then the bear was refused admission:
  its worst-case reservation ($2.90) plus the spend exceeded the cap. The run
  became data-only. A retry cannot raise a job's recorded cap, so the $0.44 was
  wasted. Worst-case reservations per request are: Haiku research $2.90, Sonnet
  5.5 research $26.36, Opus 5.5 research $52.64, judge $5.28 (Sonnet floor) or
  $10.56 (Opus). A feasibility check before the first paid request is being
  added separately.
- **Tier 2 (Sonnet 5.5 high, TSM, $2.28).** With the rules above, every pass
  succeeded at the first attempt (no repair). The judge listed 4 recent
  developments and 5 management actions, including the capex raise and the Q4
  guidance, and wrote market structure from the 20-F, stating that no market size
  is sourced. Verification was 98.3%. The misses were verifier false positives,
  fixed here:
  - "Motive is not established", the prompt's own insider wording, was read as
    naming a person "Motive". That rejected the per-person insider lines.
  - The results release TSMC furnished on Form 6-K, cited by its sec.gov archive
    URL, was refused as a credibility source because only `edgar:` ids counted as
    filings. A document under `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/<cik>/<accession>/`
    is a filing.
  - A credibility statement that names nobody and says a record is absent ("no
    prior guidance ranges are retained") may cite the payload's own gap row. That
    row supports absence and never a number.
  - "The trailing P/E was 26.4x" did not name the P/E (TTM) record. "Trailing
    P/E" and "trailing price to earnings" are now readings of it.
  - Not changed: one claim stating ROIC and its spread over WACC against one cited
    figure stays unverified, because one figure cannot bind two quantities.
- **Stamps.** Pipeline stage-c-1.6.23. Report spec and payload are unchanged.

## D-183 - Refuse a paid run before its first request when a cap can never admit it (2026-11-03)

The first paid test (D-182) ran under a $3 job cap. The bull analyst spent $0.44.
Then the bear's research request was refused admission, because its worst-case
reservation ($2.90) plus the spend exceeded the cap. The judge's worst-case
section reservation on the Sonnet 5.5 floor ($5.28) could never have fitted
either. The run became data-only, and a retry keeps the job's recorded cap
(D-120), so the $0.44 bought nothing. Nothing checked, before money was spent,
whether the run could finish.

- **Decision.** Before a run's first paid request, and before a resumed run's
  first new one, Metis prices every reservation the rest of the run will ask for.
  It uses the same functions and models admission uses: each pass lease, each
  analyst's research and writing requests, each synthesize section and any
  billable verify. If the largest one cannot fit the per-job cap (counting what
  the job has spent and has in flight) or the room left under the rolling cap,
  nothing is sent. The run ends as a data-only report at $0. The report and the
  step details name the pass, the model, the worst-case reservation, the cap that
  blocks it and the smallest cap that would admit it. Subscription connections
  reserve nothing and are never refused. Reservation formulas, admission
  accounting and cap defaults are unchanged.
- **Kept: a retry does not raise the recorded cap (D-120).** The check also runs
  on retry, so a retry that cannot finish spends nothing, and the disclosure says
  to raise the setting and start a new report.
- **Limit.** The check is necessary, not sufficient. Earlier requests spend real
  money before the largest one is admitted, so a cap just above the largest
  reservation can still stop a run part-way. `docs/CLAUDE-USAGE.md` gives the
  per-model reservations and a practical cap: about the largest reservation plus
  $10.
- **Worst-case reservations per request** (registry snapshot 2026-10-03, request
  mode): Haiku 4.5 research $2.90 and judge $5.28 on Sonnet 5.5; Sonnet 5.5
  research $26.36; Opus 5.5 research $52.64 and judge $10.56. Observed complete
  runs cost $1.62 (Haiku) and $2.28 (Sonnet 5.5 high).
- **Built** by a delegated Claude Opus 5.5 agent (extra-high effort). Tests cover
  a judge reservation above the cap, the observed $3 Haiku case, a fitting cap,
  rolling headroom, retry under a raised setting, and subscription connections.
  The refusal tests fail without the change; the controls pass either way.
- **Stamps.** Pipeline stage-c-1.6.24.

## D-184 - Annual filing sections recovered from bounded filing evidence (2026-11-03)

The 33-company panel lacked a filing section for 9 issuers, so their analysts saw
no filed risk factors, business description or MD&A. Examples: ASML's integrated
annual report maps 20-F items to chapters through a cross-reference table; NVO
uses a subordinate "D." risk heading; JNJ's Item 1A lost to a cybersecurity
cross-reference; INTC links page ranges from its contents; CAT's Part I link is
misbound.

- **Decision.** New recovery paths run only after the existing layers fail. They
  extract a section only when its start and end are proved by the filing's own
  structure:
  - a cross-reference table's destination, up to the nearest following
    destination at the same structural level;
  - a subordinate heading;
  - linked page ranges, with the closing item row in the same table;
  - a corrected contents link.

  A section ends at the next later item heading, whatever its wording. Recovery
  is withheld when an endpoint page is claimed by another item, when a linked
  table-of-contents line would start it, or when the closing boundary is not
  proved. An EX-13 redirect keeps priority over recovery. Parses are cached per
  document, and recovery honours the filing time budget. There is no
  ticker-specific code.
- **Effect on the frozen replay** (266 section slots across 38 snapshots, cached
  filings, against main at 62af738b):
  - All 212 sections that extracted before are byte-identical.
  - 8 sections are recovered: ASML risk factors, SAP business and MD&A, NVO risk
    factors, BABA risk factors, SONY MD&A, JNJ risk factors and CAT business.
  - INTC's business and MD&A stay withheld because a shared endpoint page is
    claimed by another item.
  - ASML's business and MD&A stay withheld because their dispersed mappings
    cannot be proved complete.
  - XOM stays withheld: the successor has no annual filing in the cache.
- **Independent review (2026-11-03).** Three medium and three low findings were
  fixed before merge, each with a test that fails without it:
  - a boundary skipped over an unrecognised next-item title;
  - a two-table index returned a partial MD&A;
  - endpoint pages shared with another item;
  - a linked risk table-of-contents line;
  - EX-13 precedence;
  - the reference-table end boundary.
- **Built** by delegated Codex agents (GPT-6.1 Sol, extra-high effort). 64
  recovery tests and eight trimmed public fixtures.
- **Stamps.** Payload 1.66.0: recovered text reaches the analysts for the
  affected filers.

## D-185 - Tier 3 paid test and PR #88 review: complete an incomplete case; three boundary fixes (2026-11-03)

**Tier 3 paid test.** ASML on Opus 5.5 at high effort, on the build verified for
PR #88 (report #4 in the isolated test data directory, $3.03).

- Fetch, validation and compute succeeded. The bear case succeeded: 17 thesis
  claims, 41 drivers, 14 risks and 5 catalysts.
- The bull's research succeeded ($1.02, 8 searches, 13,567 characters of dated,
  sourced notes).
- The bull's written case was a schema-valid skeleton twice: one revenue claim
  and every other section empty. Both requests ended normally (`end_turn`),
  after about 7,400 thinking tokens and 343 characters of text. The content
  check (D-113) rejected both, so synthesis and verification were skipped and the
  report is data-only.
- The same skeleton appeared on NVDA #48 (Opus 5.5, medium) and the FIGR
  high-effort run (D-162). There the one repair recovered it.

**Root cause: the request schema.** The analyst request schema required
`sourceId` beside `source` on every claim and evidence number. A first diagnosis
blamed the repair wording (below), but a retry on that fix wrote the same
skeleton twice more ($0.86). A probe then rebuilt the exact writing request from
the job's frozen inputs (payload fingerprint `1.66.0:16a8bbce`, matching the run)
and the saved bull research, and sent it with summarized thinking:

- **As sent.** The reasoning planned a full case: the thesis, the MATCH Act,
  China and customer-concentration risks, catalysts, evidence tags and a null
  price target with its conditions. It ended "I'll write the output in JSON".
  The output was the same one-claim skeleton, with `sourceId: "x"`.
- **The same request without `sourceId` in the schema.** A complete case: 17
  thesis claims, 30 drivers, 26 risks, 6 catalysts, 20 evidence numbers and
  6 price-target conditions (23,965 characters, inside the 24,000 cap).
- **The same request with no schema.** Also complete.

The analyst has no second identity to give beside `source`. It wrote a
placeholder and closed the case: 5 of 5 skeletons with the field, 1 of 1 complete
case without it. This matches NVDA #48 and #49, whose four first attempts carried
`sourceId: ""` (D-114), and the earlier bull skeletons. The three probe requests
cost $2.09.

- **Decision.** The analyst request schema omits `sourceId`, and the analyst
  cites through `source`. A parsed claim without `sourceId` already cites its
  `source` (D-114), and the stored ASML bear case has none after normalization.
  The Zod schema still accepts the field, so stored cases parse.
- **Not changed.** The judge's request schema keeps `sourceId`; no judge failure
  points to it.

**Confirmed on the paid build.** A Retry of the ASML job on the build without
`sourceId` reused the frozen inputs, the bear case and the bull's saved research.
It completed report #6:

- **Bull.** Written on the first attempt ($0.79).
- **Judge.** Three sections ($2.03, cache reads after the first).
- **Verification.** Deterministic, $0.
- **Job total.** $6.71 across every attempt.

The report has:

- **Verification rate:** 99.6%.
- **Score and value:** composite 67.38 (grade C); DCF value USD 962.12 against
  a USD 1,566.26 price.
- **Sections:** 5 dated recent developments and 7 management actions. The
  competitors (Applied Materials and KLA) are cited from the risk factors that
  D-184 recovered. The market size is stated once as unsourced. There are 5
  catalysts and 7 risks.

**Audit follow-ups (not changed in this round):**

- **Uncheckable headline claims.** Some executive-summary claims cite the right
  record, but the verifier cannot bind their wording, so they show as unchecked
  (`text-context-mismatch`). Examples: "ADS price", "DCF base-case value",
  "reverse DCF implies year-one revenue growth over TTM" and "weighted projected
  revenue for the 12 months ending". TSM report #3 had the same class. These need
  producer-bound wording, as D-182 added for "trailing P/E".
- **Buyback magnitude.** "Buybacks ... were EUR 4.07 billion" against the
  `buybacks (negative)` record is marked contradicted under D-160, which requires
  signed cash outflows to match the signed record. The sentence states the amount
  correctly as a magnitude. Accepting a magnitude with explicit outflow wording,
  or prompting the judge to write the signed figure, needs its own decision.
- **ASML sections still withheld.** The business and MD&A sections stay withheld
  (D-184). The CEO and CFO cards are not assessed for lack of attributable
  payload rows.

**Secondary: the repair wording.** The repair turn said "Fix EXACTLY these issues and
re-emit the full ANALYST_CASE JSON — same evidence, same citations, corrected
fields only". The echoed output said "repair this JSON in place — do not start
over". An empty `keyDrivers` or `risksToCase` cannot be filled without new claims,
so the instruction contradicted the rejection. The model changed only the
placeholder `sourceId` ("x" to "") and returned the same skeleton. That wording
is right for a format error, such as a bad date, which is what it was written for.

- **Decision.** A rejection from the content check is marked "the case is
  incomplete:". Its repair turn now says the case was rejected as incomplete, not
  for its format. It asks the model to fill each named section with sourced claims
  from the payload and the supplied research, keep each correct claim it already
  wrote, and state a specific evidence limitation instead of leaving a section
  empty. The echoed output says "incomplete: keep its correct claims and write the
  missing sections in full".
- **Unchanged.** Format errors keep the fix-in-place wording. The cached payload
  turn, tools and schema stay byte-identical, so the repair still reads the cache.
- **Kept.** The wording still contradicted the rejection, so it is fixed too,
  but on its own it did not recover the ASML case.
- **Tests.**
  - The analyst request schema has no `sourceId`, the judge's keeps it, and a
    stored case parses with or without it. This fails without the change.
  - Repair turns: one built from the exact ASML feedback, one control for a
    format error, and a runner test for the incomplete marker on the echoed
    output. All three fail without the change.

**PR #88 review (Codex, eight P2 findings over six rounds, plus the related gaps
found in the same review of the end search), each with a test that fails without
the fix:**

- **Linked page ranges (D-184).** A page that another item claims strictly
  inside a mapped range now withholds recovery, as an endpoint does. Example:
  INTC Business pages 3-5 with Item 1A mapped to page 4.
- **Reference-table recovery (D-184).** A heading line holding a hyperlink can
  no longer prove a chapter's start or end, matching the structured-item path.
- **Prose references as section ends (D-184, second review round).** A paragraph
  that opens with a later item's reference no longer ends the section. Examples:
  "Item 1A. Risk Factors below discusses ..." and "Item 1A of this report
  describes ...". Text that opens in lowercase, or that continues the item's
  standard title in lowercase words, is prose. A variant or nonstandard title,
  or a standard title with a parenthetical, still ends the section. The exact
  standard title ends it in any capitalization ("Item 1A. risk factors.", third
  review round), so capitalization alone cannot make recovery absorb the next
  item. The existing
  tests for singular and plural market-risk titles, "Directors and employees" and
  a 320-character title still pass.
- **Adjacent next-item heading (D-184, fourth review round).** A next-item heading
  that starts exactly where the requested heading ends was passed over, because
  element ends are exclusive and the search required a later start. The next
  item's discussion was then accepted as the requested section. The search now
  accepts a heading at that position, so the section is empty and the stub check
  withholds it. The 20-F risk path is fixed the same way.
- **Next-item headings the end search did not see (D-184, fifth review round,
  widened).** Codex found a complete next-item heading in a single-cell layout
  row that was not an end boundary, so Business absorbed the risk discussion. The
  same review of the end search found three more forms it missed:
  - a colon or a dash after the item number ("Item 1A: Risk Factors", "ITEM
    1A—RISK FACTORS");
  - a number-only cell followed by a colon;
  - a heading wrapped in a name anchor.

  The sixth round found a heading split across cells ("Item | 1A. | Risk
  Factors."). The row rules were then replaced by one rule: a row of one to four
  cells with no link reads as its non-empty cell texts in order. The same pass
  added headings in list items and other block elements, and a Part prefix
  ("PART I — ITEM 1A.").

  End proof now has its own parser and is deliberately broader than start proof.
  Absorbing the next item is the error to avoid; an early end can only shorten
  the section or leave it a withheld stub. A row or heading holding a link is
  still contents, and prose references are still not headings. Start proof is
  unchanged.
- **Pre-launch budget check (D-183).** It now counts an expired lease the way
  admission's sweep records it: presumed spend at its reservation, dated at its
  acquisition, or nothing when its request already settled or was presumed.
  Before, it counted every stored lease as live, so with a rolling window shorter
  than the lease lifetime it could refuse a run that admission would admit. The
  sweep and the check now share one function.
- **Replay.** The frozen 38-snapshot replay is unchanged by every extractor
  fix in these rounds: 266 of 266 slots are identical, with 220 sections
  extracted.

- **Stamps.** Pipeline stage-c-1.6.25. Payload 1.66.0 and report spec 1.60.0
  are unchanged.

## D-186 - Evidence-backed valuation coverage and explicit withholding reasons (2026-11-03)

The 2026-11-03 frozen census at main `56886dad` valued 20 of 33 companies.
The [evidence report](2026-11-03-valuation-coverage.md) traces all 13 remaining
companies to their exact rule, input, source and disposition, and records every
before/after fair value, WACC, DCF per share and composite.

- **NIKE: equal class economics, not missing economics.** Its retained 10-K
  `0000320187-26-000088` states there are no differences in Class A/B dividend,
  liquidation preferences or participation rights. Read that whole sentence as
  equality. The 10-Q `0000320187-26-000193` counts both classes at 2026-09-28:
  281,387,752 + 1,203,921,077 = 1,485,308,829. The same filing's balance sheet
  enumerates exactly those classes. Extend D-154's retained-cover rule to this
  equally participating, non-ADR case: apply the disclosed same-price
  approximation to every class without requiring a named quoted class. Equal
  units make the class name irrelevant to the arithmetic; voting-price
  differences remain unmodelled. A recent annual rights statement can remain
  in force through an interim filing with the identical complete class set,
  for at most 400 days and without contrary retained terms. No older count is
  carried forward. Duplicate/missing/extra classes, mixed dates, source/issuer
  mismatch, newer unresolved filings or intervening/unresolved splits refuse
  the fallback. Existing accepted evidence remains first choice.
- **NVO: an outstanding-share synonym.** The SEC FY2025 filing
  `0000353278-26-000012` tags `ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesOutstanding` (4.444B),
  with no eligible DEI count. Admit it as a fallback synonym under D-178's
  existing age/identity, 1% ratio agreement and independent weighted-average
  corroboration. Filed basic weighted shares are 4.443B versus provider
  4.447851B; quoted shares 4.420890725B agree with market cap / price. Both
  constructions establish 1 ordinary per ADS. DEXDNUS 6.6946 DKK/USD dated
  2026-10-30 translates all valuation monetary levels once. Issued/authorized
  shares and monetary treasury stock are not outstanding-count substitutes.
- **EXPE: the missing operating maturity cancels.** Filing
  `0001324424-26-000053` proves current borrowings zero, noncurrent borrowings
  USD 5.459B and a noncurrent operating-lease observation USD 226M at
  2026-06-30. The retained vendor total 5.685B reconciles to those components.
  Extending the existing FCX partial-lease rule is appropriate: reconstruct
  that partial calculation view with exact same-filing provenance, then
  cancel the embedded operating portion under the default lease-excluded
  convention. No missing maturity is zero-filled or called a complete total.
  The lease-inclusive switch still refuses it. Extra borrowings, finance
  leases (including legacy maturity synonyms), contradictory/mixed/future
  facts, component refusals and independent debt-collapse refusals still
  withhold; normal debt plausibility/aggregate checks run afterward. This
  supersedes D-179's EXPE disposition only for that proved cancellation case.
- **Refusals remain meaningful.** AAPL's unexplained debt collapse (D-174),
  MCD's million-fold tagged
  share-unit disagreement, TM/SAP's disputed current count ratios, SONY's
  stale count, BABA's split/count contradictions, and TSM's missing current NCI
  profit allocation remain withheld. No tolerance was widened, refused
  operand was zero-filled, or stale balance/NCI allocation substituted.
- **Model boundaries remain.** ORCL and TSLA fail D-102's terminal/explicit-PV
  domain test. INTC and SONY trigger the loss-making overlay. A negative net
  income is not proof of structurally negative free cash flow: the disclosure
  now names the actual trigger and selected basis, and calls for a separately
  supported turnaround forecast. Missing MD&A does not withhold INTC's value.
  No new valuation model is built.
- **Explain the actual input refusal.** Headline fair-value reasons now carry
  the underlying debt refusal behind missing capital, the failed currency/ADS
  evidence, or the original share-unit disagreement, instead of only the
  downstream symptom. This changes explanation, not the remaining refusals.
- **Measured result.** Coverage rises 20 -> 23 of 33. EXPE: WACC 9.607259385%
  -> 9.757796877%, DCF USD 257.796844275/share, composite 61.77 -> 63.11.
  NKE: WACC unavailable ->
  9.028091663%, DCF USD 41.094290265/share, composite 48.97 -> 51.35. NVO:
  WACC unavailable -> 7.033602931%, DCF USD 93.387500428/ADS, composite
  60.34 -> 69.11. Every previously valued company's fair value, WACC and
  DCF/share is identical at full precision. COST's composite intentionally
  moves 61.97 -> 61.30 as proved partial-lease financing restores historical
  EV multiples and their grading observation: EV/EBITDA rank 73.8692 over 12
  quarters, valuation completeness 0.4 -> 0.7. The valuation aspect rises
  15 -> 25.21, but its added below-neutral weight lowers the composite.
  No other company moves in the four compared metrics.
- **Analyst qualifications.** NKE's USD 41.09 versus USD 38.22 depends on the
  existing five-year-median 11.92% margin fallback, not an admitted current
  operating margin. NVO's USD 93.39 versus USD 40.105 (+132.86%) is a material
  assumption-risk flag: the model starts at +11.76% growth with no admitted
  consensus, while reverse DCF implies -14.97%. It is a conditional historical
  economics case, not evidence of a mispriced stock. The report records unit,
  bridge, reverse-solve and sensitivity checks; no value was tuned to price.
  EXPE's USD 257.80 versus USD 286.63 passes the bridge/reverse checks; the
  disclosed house sales-to-capital cap and its larger period-average diluted
  denominator remain material assumptions.
- **Tests and versions.** Every numerical repair and disclosure repair has an
  observed failing regression before the change. The retained class fixture is
  trimmed public SEC evidence. Constants are intentionally not changed here.
  Release needs new Stage B, fair-value and scenario-target method stamps and
  a payload version for changed deterministic inputs/disclosures. No schema or
  pipeline orchestration change requires a report-spec or pipeline bump.
  Verification results and any environmental limitations are in the evidence
  report; saved bundles/reports are unchanged.

## D-187 - Producer-bound headline readings and statement outflow magnitudes (2026-11-03)

Revised by D-263: outflow scope now follows explicit producer metadata, with the historical statement contract retained.

**Decision.** Correct numeric prose may use an equivalent name only under its
producing record's contract. Add readings for ADS quote prices, DCF base-case
per-share values, reverse-DCF year-one revenue growth over starting TTM
revenue, weighted/scenario projections, EV/EBITDA, settled closes, five-year
weighted-average diluted-share changes and TTM standardized FCF. Projection
readings retain the scenario, metric, endpoint and units; the forward EPS
producer means operating EPS and its FCF producer means unlevered FCF.
The "ADS price" reading binds the quoted price only: the numeric record does
not carry the depositary-share flag, so whether the instrument is an ADS is a
qualitative assertion that stays unchecked (integration review).
Grade annotations in the forms ", grade B" and ", in band B" are checked
against the score's house band before being masked. Completeness assertions
are not inferred from a score.

The additions use producer-bound `forms.add(...)` readings and the existing
typed-context hook. Window spelling is normalized only for the producing
projection/FCF records, retaining the stated date for the ordinary period
check. A reverse-DCF phrase must explicitly name year one and the TTM baseline
before its baseline words are treated as its denominator. The general metric,
period, direction, currency, rounding and unit rules are unchanged. No ticker
or company name participates.

**Revises D-160: outflow amounts.** A buyback amount is conventionally stated
as a positive magnitude. For negative, currency-valued provider records under
`payload.statements.cash-flow-(annual|quarterly).<date>.*` labeled exactly
`buybacks (negative)` or `capex (negative)`, prose naming buybacks, share
repurchases, capital expenditure or capex may state the absolute value.
The annotations "(cash outflow)" and "of cash outflow" are permitted.
Inflow wording, direction words, every other record and nonnegative records
retain signed matching. Existing signed outflow prose remains supported.
This supersedes D-160's requirement that every such amount print the record's
negative sign; it does not introduce general absolute-value matching.

**Evidence and tests.** The paid META #2, TSM #3 and ASML #6 reports were
examined from the isolated database opened with `readonly: true` and
`fileMustExist: true`. Frozen bundles and saved judge outputs were replayed
through `runVerifyPass`, before and after, with the same retained research URL
identities and no provider/model calls. Newly validated claims: META 4, TSM 4,
ASML 21 (29 total); no previously validated claim regressed. The classes are:
projection wording 10, DCF base-case value 2, ADS price 1, reverse DCF 2,
statement buyback magnitudes 3, EV/EBITDA 1, settled close 1, five-year share
change 3, TTM FCF 2 and checked grade annotations 4. Full inventories, rejected
claims, replay logs and every newly validated claim are retained under `tmp/`.

Tests were written first: the final regression set fails 24 tests against the
unchanged verifier and passes all 106 tests in the two affected files with
the change. Controls retain wrong values, periods, metrics, currencies,
per-share bases, projection scenarios/definitions, reverse-DCF horizons and
baselines, grades, annualized share changes, cash inflows and directions.
Multi-figure claims, ranges citing only a midpoint and out-of-scope signed
cash-flow records remain unvalidated. Tests:
`stageC.claimEvidence.headline.test.ts` and `stageC.claimEvidence.figr.test.ts`.

**Stamps.** A `PIPELINE_VERSION` bump to stage-c-1.6.26, applied at integration, for changed Stage C
verification outcomes. No payload, report-spec or Stage B stamp change is
required: their contracts, stored bytes and calculations are unchanged.

## D-188 - Calibrated foreign revenue, proved operating income and corroborated units (2026-11-03)

**Decision.** Repair the valuation inputs generally, without choosing any
assumption or tolerance to approach a quote. The complete 33-company fresh
baseline/replay, per-company causes, eight-company sanity checks, fail-first
evidence and verification are in [the evidence report](2026-11-03-valuation-inputs.md).

- **Revises D-57 for revenue totals only.** With an admitted foreign valuation
  basis and withheld issuer-currency inheritance, an estimate without its own
  currency can calibrate to filed annual reporting-currency revenue at the
  same fiscal end, available at cutoff. Latest overlap must agree within 3%,
  its listing-currency reading must fail beyond 6%, FX must separate the
  readings, and every other overlap in the last three filed fiscal years must
  agree within 10%. Failure names its test. Own-row currency still wins; EPS,
  per-share rows and targets remain withheld. The existing one-spot FX,
  D-65 consensus quality, D-60 precedence, calendarization and clamps apply.
  Stage C labels revenue by the same proof. Notes/manifest name the year,
  estimate, filed amount and tolerance.
- **Revises the operating-basis refusal, retaining D-164/FIGR.** A provider
  operating numerator may agree with SEC-derived operating income on the
  exact revenue basis, or be paired in its retained original provider row
  with revenue agreeing with filed revenue, for the same issuer, currency,
  fiscal interval and filing date. Explicit revenue/numerator conflicts,
  contrary directly tagged EBIT and missing period/basis proof still refuse.
  No gross-profit/expense classification follows from an admitted numerator.
  FIGR's pre-interest provider numerator remains refused. All existing
  downstream consumers receive newly admitted history; scores are not frozen.
- **Revises D-58/D-60's margin fallback order.** Guidance and the admitted
  trailing pair lead, then the latest admitted annual margin whose fiscal
  year ended within 15 calendar months of cutoff, then the five-year median.
  Median seeds are historical, never described as current. Fade, one-off
  normalization and margin ceilings are unchanged.
- **Revises D-179 and D-186's MCD disposition.** A direct SEC share fact may
  be treated as a filer scaling error only at exactly 1,000 or 1,000,000,
  within 0.1% of provider count, independently within 3% of a filed DEI cover
  within 100 days of period end and within 3% of market cap / price. Identity,
  latest-fact, exact-period, currency, cutoff and split checks remain. Repairs
  are calculation-view-only and disclosed; correct facts are not scaled.
- **Revises D-102 E-5 and D-186's TSM disposition narrowly.** First derive a
  current allocation from filed consolidated profit less profit attributable
  to owners of the parent when both share one filing, period and currency.
  Otherwise a last filed annual allocation can size E-5 only within 24 calendar
  months of cutoff, absolute NCI share of positive consolidated profit below
  1%, and book NCI below 1% of computed consolidated equity value. Deduct book
  NCI with the stale basis disclosed. Missing allocation is never zero;
  larger/older/invalid and redeemable claims retain refusal.
- **Revises D-178/D-186's SAP count disposition.** A nonstandard DEI cover
  ratio may defer to the independent standard weighted-average construction
  within 1% only when the cover equals same-filing, same-period issued shares
  within 0.1%. It may include treasury and is not substituted for outstanding
  shares. Other identity, split, FX and debt gates remain. SAP's historical
  debt refusals persist, but do not block its complete current/bridge balances.
- **Tests and stamps.** Every new positive admission, fallback and cutoff
  repair has observed failing evidence before implementation, with negative
  controls and the existing FIG/FIGR regressions retained. New fixtures are
  synthetic. Full verification and honest conditional-model qualifications
  are in the linked report. Stamps, with D-186 and D-187: Stage B, fair value
  and scenario targets `VALUATION_INPUTS_45`, payload 1.67.0, pipeline
  stage-c-1.6.26. Stored reports are unchanged.

  Integration review: the listing-currency and FX separation test is 6%, not
  the 10% first written. The 3% agreement already rejects the other reading,
  and at 10% a euro drifting below about 1.11 would have switched analyst
  revenue off for euro reporters. Known limit: at this rate the DCF is still far
  above the quote for NVO (USD 76.85 against 40.105), because the model holds
  its roughly 42% margin at a 7.03% WACC; the report's reverse DCF shows the gap.

## D-189 - Latest admitted financial book and producer-bound headline wording (2026-11-03)

**Opening book (Task A).** Decouple the financial-route opening balance from
the availability of a complete trailing return. Select the newest quarterly
balance newer than the fiscal-year book only with positive common equity,
explicit equity and preferred operands (also goodwill and other intangibles
for tangible common equity), matching currency and date, filing available at
cutoff, no operand conflict, and an admitted diluted divisor ending on that
same date. Field-level evidence must agree on period, units and filing cutoff.
Refuse negative adjustments and contradictory filing/acceptance dates.
Otherwise retain the annual calculation and disclose the reason, including an
info missing-data entry. No undisclosed adjustment becomes zero.

This revises D-102/C-10's coupling of return and opening book, retaining its
reason: a newer complete trailing return is more representative than a
distorted fiscal year. Return selection, CAPM, terminal evidence, carry, payout

the existing 1-200-day CoE roll start at the selected book. C-10's fiscal-return
alternative keeps its own fiscal-year book, date and preferred claims. A bank's
P/TBV reads the selected balance and retains the return's own date; other routes
keep their fiscal tangible balance. If the quarterly book is refused, the prior
path stands exactly, including a trailing start's own dated book (integration
review: the first version fell back to the older annual book and moved the
alternative; nine existing regressions caught it). Stored reports remain immutable.

## D-190 - Executive cards reflect dated management decisions (2026-11-04)

- **Evidence and root cause.** The saved judge and verification artifacts for
  reports 6 (ASML), 7 (JPM) and 8 (NVO) separate three problems. JPM's judge
  proposed B execution grades for both officers on a validated five-year
  diluted-share-count trend; the narrow typed-metric gate discarded that
  metric and overwrote the more specific reasons. ASML's judge and NVO's CFO
  supplied no execution evidence and no tenure start, so their unassessed
  grades were honest. NVO's CEO retained C because typed operating cash flow
  and repurchases qualified under the earlier result-only rule. None of the
  cards consumed `leadership.managementActions` or the company outlook
  discussion. Fetched SEC archive URLs in ASML/NVO guidance were additionally
  refused when absent from the payload citation registry, despite D-182's
  source-class correction. Many action figures were genuinely still unchecked.
- **Decision.** Relevant dated office decisions and the retained company
  guidance discussion appear on each CEO/CFO card across live, Markdown and
  print views. Original company/board attribution and JUDGMENT claims remain;
  unchecked context is labelled and rejected claims are excluded. The card
  states the missing tenure, decision or guidance comparison. This is useful
  context, not proof of the person's contribution or a new personal record.
- **Execution admission.** A proposed letter can use a dated management action
  when the card repeats its FACT and citation in reasoning or capital-allocation
  evidence, and each action fact quotes a whole sentence exactly as the cited
  retained filing/transcript writes it, with no failed check. A whole-sentence
  quotation proves figures, wording and qualifications together, so one that
  drops a trailing condition does not match; the numeric check alone cannot, and it
  reads a true sentence as ambiguous when the amount recurs. Real filings write
  dates out and use a dollar sign, so both forms are accepted: JPM's 10-Q
  sentence on its USD 50 billion authorization replays through this route once
  a tenure start is supplied. The event date is the sentence's only date or its
  opening "On <date>", never an effective date, and must fall within an evidenced office
  tenure, from explicit `titleSince` or an exact retained appointment sentence. Unknown/conflicting dates and divisional,
  deputy or staff authority fail closed. The assessment concerns decisions and
  outcomes during that tenure, not personal skill. A completed authorization
  retains its suspension qualification and is never presented as an executed
  repurchase or realized return. No letter is manufactured if the judge left
  the evidence ungraded. The new admission is additive: if it refuses a
  candidate, the existing typed-metric gate and its original reasons remain
  exactly as before. No additional fallback is introduced.
- **Reasons retained.** D-59 made an unreachable gate usable; D-63 admitted
  company guidance during an evidenced CEO/CFO tenure; D-66 barred pay and
  unknown metric semantics from unlocking grades; D-163 distinguished company
  outcomes from a personal record; D-177 retained dated company/board actions.
  Those protections and the existing typed execution admission remain. A
  share-count trend does not satisfy the new decision contract. Historical
  grades and verification marks remain immutable. Withheld grade rationales
  stay withheld when ungraded office-context cards are expanded.
- **Credibility.** The typed guidance comparison contract remains. Issuance or
  revision alone, unmatched accounting bases and a partial year plus a Q4
  forecast cannot establish a completed guidance record. A known fetched SEC
  archive document is now an eligible filing citation without needing a second
  payload-registry row; neither the URL nor that eligibility validates its
  contents. The named-person restriction remains.
- **Offline result.** Saved judges, their generation-matched frozen bundles and
  saved fetched-URL telemetry were replayed through current-code calculation,
  assembly and deterministic verification for reports 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8. No model
  ran. JPM's cards each expose 7 relevant actions, ASML's expose 7/6, NVO's 5/4;
  the company guidance discussion is carried with its original status. No new
  letters are supportable from these saved outputs. NVO's CEO C remains under
  the unchanged typed execution gate, in both the replay and the stored report.
  Reports 2 and 3 still parse and export. All stored JSON was re-read unchanged.
- **Validation and limits.** Test-first regressions cover title/pay-only,
  company-result-only decision candidates, missing/outside tenure,
  rejected/unchecked claims, wrong office,
  no later actual, invented wording/date, unbound grades, SEC lookalikes and
  authorization qualifications. Typecheck, changed-file ESLint and related
  tests and the integrator's `--changed origin/main --passWithNoTests` sweep
  are the gate; the full `npm run verify` is deliberately omitted.
  Future model compliance with exact dated decision/card binding and tenure
  instructions requires a paid run. No paid/provider/network calls were made.
  The roster supplied no tenure start for any of the three reports, so this
  route stays closed for most officers until tenure is read from filings. The
  judge keeps its typed-metric instructions, the only route that has produced a
  letter in a saved report.
- **Stamps required at integration.** Advance the report spec for the changed
  executive-grade meaning and the Stage C pipeline stamp for prompt/verifier
  behavior. No payload shape, Stage B, valuation method or score-band change is
  needed. This implementation intentionally changes no version constants.

## D-191 - Recover explicit annual-report page references with honest coverage (2026-11-04)

The frozen 33-company panel retained four missing business/MD&A sections:
INTC 10-K Items 1/7 and ASML 20-F Items 4/5. PEP, DIS and EXPE retained
underlying financial-note item failures; MSFT, MCD and ORCL had separate

first lines are in the [evidence report](https://github.com/eligorelick/Metis/blob/bda87e4c0b575fdf4af2a4e31a66854c9c42337b/docs/audit/2026-11-04-foreign-sections.md).

- **Shared pages revise D-184/D-185.** A filing's explicit incorporation of
  the same pages into two items is not an exclusive-ownership conflict. Admit
  the requested ranges only when every endpoint link, intervening printed
  page and closing item row is proved. Merge repeated/overlapping ranges;
  disclose shared pages in extraction diagnostics. INTC explicitly incorporates
  segment results into Business and MD&A, and financial-note pages into MD&A.
- **Point pages are excerpts, not complete chapters.** For dispersed 20-F
  mappings, resolve every reference across repeated column headers and merged
  item-caption cells. Each destination must uniquely identify its printed,
  closed physical page before the index. The unnumbered cover is admitted only
  when explicitly mapped as Cover page 1 and its form/annual-report text agrees.
  Keep only mapped pages; never infer a chapter end from an unrelated link or
  slice to EOF. Label the returned text and payload title as mapped-page
  excerpts with the complete item not recovered. This is an explicit partial
  evidence route, not a relaxation of the complete-section proof.
- **Wrong text remains withheld.** Reject contents/index pages, wrong-page,
  duplicate, missing or external destinations, malformed/open mappings and
  truncated source stubs. Resolve but omit navigation-only chapter dividers,
  disclosing their page numbers. Missing references refuse the whole mapping;
  no subset can silently stand in for it. Existing EX-13 precedence, hidden
  markup handling, ordinary extraction and deadline checks remain.
- **Absence reasons.** Unresolved 10-K financial-statement index stubs now
  retain the actual source reference and explain that complete section bounds
  were not proved. A 40-F is no longer sent through a purported 10-K item job:
  it explicitly requires the annual-report exhibit from the filing index.
  Automated 40-F exhibit selection is not added.
- **Effect.** INTC recovers both complete mapped-range assemblies. ASML
  supplies 11/13 unique mapped pages for Items 4/5; its Item 4 navigation page
  13 is omitted. ASML's complete chapters remain unproved. PEP, DIS and EXPE
  notes remain gaps with specific reference reasons; the other three domestic
  notes-recognition gaps are unchanged. In 146 real-document
  section checks, successes increase from 137 to 141 and all 137 previous
  successes are byte-identical. No stored report or input was rewritten.
- **Stamps required, not applied.** Advance the payload version for changed

  roster person and issuer-wide office. Optional middle initials are safe;

  needs the full named officer in the bounded passage and no competing person.

  stated period's last day for overlap checks, not an invented exact start.

  supported periods or roster starts and future filing/report dates fail closed.

  gates still decide grades; no letter or claim binding is manufactured.

  CEO C remains under the prior typed gate. The other saved judges do not bind
  the requisite quoted dated decision to a proposed grade. New grade proposals
  and the judge's response to enriched context require a separately authorized

- **Deliberate limits.** Unsupported appointment chronology, inception/same-year
  references, full-middle-name aliases, non-Latin parentheticals, suffix
  punctuation and surname biographies beyond the bounded span stay withheld.
  Microsoft CFO wording gives two dates for the same office and fails closed.
  Director timelines and first-election-to-officer tables are not inferred into

## D-193 - Scenario targets for banks and insurers (2026-11-04)

**Design recorded before implementation.** The frozen census2 panel contains
33 companies and zero financial routes (UNH remains a healthcare operator).
The supplied qpaid and final84 snapshots add JPM: qpaid price USD 337.98,
fair value USD 231.55; final84 is a second dated observation of the same bank.
Today both publish no targets and incorrectly explain the absence solely by
the lack of an FCFF path. No saved insurer or other bank exists in these
snapshot collections; synthetic bank/insurer records test the general rule.

**Method.** Reuse the existing residual-income engine, opening common book,
admitted per-share bridge and valuation-date roll. Base is the existing fair
value rounded by the same rule, never a new valuation. Require the retained
base path to reproduce the existing equity value before publishing a fan.
For banks use their own ROTE history; for insurers and mortgage REITs use
their own common-equity ROE, exactly the basis already valued. Substituting
tangible returns for an insurer's common-book model would move the base.

Take the latest five annual observations, or four when only four exist,
requiring unique dates, consecutive 330-400-day intervals, finite positive
returns throughout and a positive current return. Do not delete loss,
missing or acquisition years to improve the sample. House rule: linearly
interpolated 25th/75th percentiles, rank (n-1)*p, bound bear/bull starts;
bear start=min(base start,Q25), bull start=max(base start,Q75). This keeps
an unusual current rate inside the range without fitting anything to price.
Less than four observations, gaps, unavailable returns and any loss/zero
return refuse specifically. If even the highest return on all three paths
does not exceed cost of equity, refuse: there is no evidenced excess-return
fan. No peer, consensus or price enters the construction.

The explicit horizon N and terminal return T stay fixed. With u=t/(N-1),
base's linear remaining deviation is (1-u). Bull retains (1-u)^0.5 of a
positive starting deviation above T, and (1-u)^2 of a negative deviation;
bear reverses those exponents. These disclosed house persistence stresses
keep bull pointwise at/above base and bear at/below it even when a return is
recovering toward T. Half the deviation disappears after 75% of the explicit
interval for the slow fade and 29.29% for the fast fade (base 50%); these
are assumption stresses, not estimated persistence or calibrated quantiles.
No extra terminal excess is invented. Discount rate, complete payout path,
terminal return, continuing growth/carry, shares, book and roll remain fixed.
Payout is not stressed: return history does not establish distribution
capacity or regulatory permission. Continuing value changes only through
the book generated by the stressed return path. Convertible claims refuse
until scenario-specific conversion choices can be established, rather than
silently freezing a nonlinear equity claim. Non-finite/non-positive results,
an unreproducible base or invalid retained inputs also refuse specifically.

**Reader contract.** Use existing scenarioTargets, method
`excess-return-history`, null DCF dispersion and zero unused revenue/margin
deltas. Basis lines disclose historical observations, quartiles, exact return
and payout paths, persistence rules, fixed inputs, model-output provenance,
value date and implied target/diluted tangible-book multiples where established.
An insurer without tangible book can retain a valid common-book scenario,
but its P/TBV is withheld explicitly; common book is never relabelled tangible.
Live, Markdown and print share this disclosure and scenario assumptions;
horizons say explicit excess-return horizon. No probability or twelve-month
price forecast is implied. Old reports remain immutable and parse unchanged.
The DCF branch and its presentation are unchanged, proved by byte comparison
of every non-financial Stage B output on the frozen panel.

**Alternatives rejected.** A DCF-style growth/margin fan does not model the
financial franchise. An arbitrary +/-return or +/-CoE band fits no company
evidence and mixes business and discount-rate risk. Changing terminal carry
would layer a second unsupported franchise assumption onto the existing
terminal-evidence convention. The chosen finite-path stresses make the
business sensitivity visible while preserving that existing judgment.

**Stamps required, not applied.** Advance Stage B, scenario-target and
scenario-presentation method stamps, payload (new registered computed scenario numbers) and Stage C
pipeline (horizon/assumption presentation). No fair-value formula, report
schema, score-band or historical-report rewrite is required. This branch
intentionally changes no version constants.

**Implementation evidence.** The scenario-only book gate additionally checks
explicit, unconflicted operands in the model currency at the selected opening
book and the annual closing/opening books used by the sampled returns. It
preserves the pre-existing fair value even where that stricter gate refuses.
An undisclosed insurer intangible withholds P/TBV while its evidenced common
book can still support common-equity scenarios. The existing return helper's
average-book convention (closing book alone when no prior annual balance
exists) is retained; it is not replaced with a fabricated opening balance.

Offline frozen-input results (USD; target P/TBV uses the model's admitted
diluted divisor and 2026-09-30 tangible book):

| Saved bank observation | Price | Fair value | Bull | Base | Bear | Bull/base/bear P/TBV | Refusal |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| JPM qpaid, 2026-11-03 | 337.98 | 231.55 | 258.35 | 231.55 | 221.63 | 2.4197x / 2.1687x / 2.0758x | None |
| JPM final84, 2026-11-02 | 340.58 | 231.78 | 258.62 | 231.78 | 221.83 | 2.4223x / 2.1709x / 2.0777x | None |

The qpaid fair-value block is byte-identical to its pre-change replay; the
final84 base agrees with D-189's existing USD 231.78. Both formerly had empty
targets with the generic non-DCF suppression. Every one of the 33 census2
non-financial Stage B outputs is JSON-byte-identical before/after; validation
and input bundles are identical too. Per-company SHA-256 proofs and all replay
artifacts remain under `tmp/excess-return-scenarios/`.

**Analyst sanity check, not calibration.** Both saved observations have the
same USD 373.36 consensus (low 312, high 425). The newer bull is still 23.56%
below price and below even that consensus low. This is a large disagreement,
not an attractive-looking target range. Investigation finds a 20.6961% current
ROTE, 20.6961%/22.9195% history quartiles, 9.4595% CoE, 14.4595% terminal ROTE
and a fixed 60.3950%-82.7103% payout fade. Even bull must converge to that
terminal return. The existing reverse solve needs 36.5051% starting ROTE to
match price under the base dynamics, versus a 23.3413% maximum in the five-year
record. This is franchise-persistence/return disagreement; it is not a reason
to fit a wider fan to the quote or consensus. No assumption was tuned.

Retrospective fiscal-end market-cap/TCE observations from the same frozen
record are 2.3268x (2021), 1.9470x (2022), 2.0998x (2023), 2.5979x (2024) and
3.1490x (2025), using the last trading date at/before each year end. The new
2.0758x-2.4197x target band sits inside that historical range, below its recent
upper end. These are accounting-date cross-checks, not a trading backtest.
Today's quote divided by the model's diluted TBV/share is 3.1656x; the separate
market-cap/TCE card is 3.1363x because market cap and the model's diluted count
use different share measures. Target multiples consistently use the latter
model divisor. No real insurer or second bank is claimed as validated: only
JPM exists in the supplied frozen snapshots; synthetic insurer/bank fixtures
exercise both bases and refusals. Stored qpaid reports are read-only, still
parse and render on all three surfaces, and their saved JSON stays unchanged.

**Validation.** Seventeen initial regressions failed before implementation,
including thin history, loss years, a refused opening book, missing CoE and
returns at/below CoE. Later regressions failed before fixes for an absent
retained payout path, missing bank/insurer tangible operands and an unsupported
opening annual book in the oldest sampled return. All 24 focused tests pass,
including base/fair-value equality, recovery paths, four-year interpolation,
conversion refusal, price/WACC independence and all three report surfaces.
Node 24 typecheck and changed-file ESLint pass. The required unfiltered
`--changed origin/main --passWithNoTests` selection first passed 11,154 tests
and hit one Windows EPERM cleanup error in the corrected-CLI import subprocess
at its 10-second boundary. Its seven tests passed in isolation; the complete
same changed selection with `--maxWorkers 2` then passed all 467 files and
11,155 tests. No product or test was weakened for that host failure. Separate
`tests/risk.coverage.test.ts` (11 tests) and `tests/repository.release.test.ts`
(18 tests) pass. The release inventory initially caught the new test before
it was staged; staging it resolved that inventory mismatch. No new source or
documentation file requires an inventory entry. The full `npm run verify`
was not run. No external network/provider/model/paid call or credential read
was made; frozen-source database opens used the supplied paths with
readonly/fileMustExist (the prescribed tests create their own temporary DBs).

**Real-data check, added at integration.** The panel has no financial route, so ten
banks and insurers ran on this branch through a data-only server with no AI key, at
no cost. Six published a range (bull / base / bear, implied P/TBV where established):
BAC 40.02 / 38.44 / 37.11, 1.34-1.44x; WFC 68.92 / 67.25 / 63.34, 1.45-1.57x; MS 103.85
/ 99.96 / 85.28, 1.58-1.93x; USB 57.86 / 55.77 / 52.72, 2.00-2.20x; TRV 403.30 / 359.54
/ 229.37, 1.93-3.40x; MET 52.62 / 51.88 / 48.41, P/TBV withheld. Four refused with a
stated reason: GS (convertible claims), C (no return above the cost of equity on any
path), PGR (no payout path; no fair value either) and AIG (preferred stock missing or
conflicted). The ranges are often narrow, because a company's own recent returns bound

  notes at F-9 through the final F-43. Unlike the old appendix layout, there
  is no linked S-schedule. Its linked, unnumbered statement-group title is
  separately proved against the first numbered statement page.
- MSFT: Item 8 succeeds, but `NOTES TO FINANCI AL STATEMENTS` misses the
  literal heading regex. The fallback recognizes the closed title vocabulary
  while retaining the original bytes. The auditor title is itself split as
  `REGIST ERED`; its title plus salutation bounds the newly recognized notes.
- MCD: Item 8 succeeds. Notes begin with unnumbered Summary of Significant
  Accounting Policies. The fallback requires the immediate Nature of Business
  opening and actual consolidation disclosure, plus the existing stub guard.
- ORCL: successful slices previously supplied no recognized notes: Item 8
  begins inside Note 1 and the later complete title is `CONSOLID ATED`. The
  annual-only fallback recognizes that split title in Item 15. Its full-source
  index can independently prove page 69 and the index-of-exhibits end.

### Rule and preservation

Legacy notes and appendix-index successes take precedence. New annual-only
recognition tolerates spaces inside the closed Consolidated/Financial title
words; it never rewrites source text. Contents-page numbers immediately after
a first-note title, reference openings and truncated stubs are rejected.

The new index route reads balanced original HTML, preserves original source
offsets and requires a financial index with balance sheets and notes. Every
linked numeric or F-prefixed row must resolve to one visible same-document
target and the same unique printed page. Fragmented title/page links must all
agree. Unnumbered linked statement-group headings require their own source
heading and a numbered statement on that page. No page ranges are guessed.
A notes-group heading can supply a first-note mapping; all later mapped notes
must fall within the retained bounds. Notes require a real opening, consecutive
physical printed pages, and a closed appendix heading or a closed document
ending at a proved final printed footer. Duplicate, missing or interrupted
page evidence withholds the result. Self-closing namespaced metadata is
admitted only inside hidden metadata; visible nonvoid markup stays strict.

The original appendix evidence retains its schedule field. General financial
indexes instead record a heading/document-end boundary and last printed page.
The acquisition endpoint now accurately names a same-document financial index.

## D-198 - Material operating sales, preferred capital and independent trailing earnings (2026-11-04)

The independent frozen-input audit found three input-admission defects. This
decision changes admission rather than calibrating a target price. Acquired
snapshots and saved reports remain immutable; existing report schemas and
display adapters are unchanged.

### Rules and source evidence

1. **Independent earnings and revenue.** The old whole-TTM revenue gate
   discarded complete common earnings before the earnings-specific checks.
   Keep the admitted earnings window after the existing fiscal-period,
   currency, issuer and filing checks. Common returns can consume four
   complete common-earnings quarters without revenue. All existing
   revenue-dependent consumers retain their complete-revenue gate. A missing
   common-earnings quarter still refuses the trailing return.
2. **Material completed operating sales.** A broad disposition tag alone does
   not establish recurrence, placement or window. The house threshold is an
   individual sale gain of at least 10% of absolute operating income in the
   current admitted seed window. This is an input-materiality rule, unrelated
   to the resulting valuation. The 49-company current-seed scan touches BA
   only: its aggregate tagged TTM disposition gain is $9.688B against $9.735B
   of filed operating income; the individually evidenced event is $9.566B.
   Other current routine disposal observations stay below the threshold.
   Retained notes must identify a completed sale, date, gain and statement
   line; both that line and the operating subtotal must reconcile to
   same-filing, same-duration facts. Only a line before the operating subtotal
   qualifies. Cash-flow statements cannot establish income placement. The
   event must be inside the admitted seed window. Missing placement,
   unsupported formats, or an unexplained material remainder withholds the
   DCF. Overlapping aliases cannot count an event twice.

   Read BA's retained 2025 Note 3 and consolidated operations: Digital
   Aviation Solutions closed on 2025-10-31; its $9.566B gain was included in
   Gain on dispositions, net, above operating income. The source is
   [BA 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12927/000162828026004357/ba-20251231.htm),
   accession 0001628280-26-004357. Remove this event once from affected annual
   and quarterly calculation views. Historical margin paths, ROIC/quality,
   coverage and EBITDA multiples share the corrected operating income.
   Without separately established tax/common-holder allocation, recurring net
   earnings, EPS and tax pairs are withheld for affected periods. Filed
   earnings remain source observations; no pre-tax gain is subtracted from
   after-tax earnings, and sale proceeds are not removed again from cash.
   The existing impairment rules then leave a 0.320293% current margin and
   declining normalized history. The DCF fails its existing domain guard;
   fair value, targets, reverse DCF and sensitivity values are withheld with
   a reason naming the sale. There is no turnaround forecast.
3. **Preferred capital.** Zero displayed par with filed preferred shares,
   dividends or an aggregate liquidation claim does not establish zero senior
   capital. Use a same-balance-date filed APIC-inclusive carrying amount
   first, otherwise the same-date aggregate liquidation preference, labelled
   as the liquidation claim used for common book. Authorized shares and
   per-share preferences are not aggregate capital. Without either amount,
   withhold common book and its financial value/targets; do not restore an
   older annual book. Apply the same claim guard to common-book multiples and
   non-financial DCF/EV bridges.

   Read MET's retained June 2026 Note 13: 24,572,200 preferred shares and $31M
   quarterly/$76M year-to-date preferred dividends are disclosed. Its
   [June 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1099219/000109921926000050/met-20260630.htm)
   establishes no same-date aggregate capital amount. The filed $2.905B
   preference at 2025-12-31 is used only on that dated annual book, never on
   June 2026. MET's latest common book, financial fair value and targets are
   withheld. The historical zero-line scan also flags ORCL, EXPE, PGR, AIG,
   O and CRWV; these are source-date qualifications, not invented current
   claims. In non-financials the flagged retained points are historical, so
   this panel does not demonstrate an additional available current DCF being
   withdrawn. The non-financial current-bridge case is covered synthetically.

## D-201 - A composite that lost an aspect says so (2026-11-04)

The composite counts an unscored aspect at the neutral midpoint. That rule is
stated, and it stops sparse favorable data creating an extreme grade. It also
means that withholding poor evidence can raise the number: MET rose from 43.93
to 53.14 when its valuation was withheld (D-198), and BABA rose 0.56 when
unsupported earnings left its score (D-200). Neither is a better conclusion
about the company.

Changing the formula, or adding a penalty for missing evidence, would pick a
number with no evidence behind it, so the score stays as computed. The composite
note, which every surface prints, now names each unscored aspect that carries
weight and says its weight counts as neutral, and that the score is not directly
comparable with a company scored on that aspect. This is computed at display
time from the stored aspects, so saved reports get it without being rewritten.
Aspects the route gives no weight to are not mentioned, and fully scored
composites read exactly as before. No score, band or stamp changes.

## D-197 - Check AI-written figures and bind executive grades to office tenure (2026-11-04)

The independent C/D audit demonstrated unchecked financial figures in plain
reader strings, execution grades supported by results before appointment,
model-authored tenure printed as fact, acronym expansion false failures and a
data-only gap count that included informational entries.

The deterministic verifier walks reader prose outside sourced claims and
traced numbers. It checks context first using the existing metric, period,
currency, unit and displayed-precision contracts. If an identified metric and
period record disagree, a visible "Differs from the record" note names stated
and recorded values even when the stated value exists elsewhere. If the value
is absent everywhere in retained evidence, a visible "Not matched to a source"
note names it. A found value with unconfirmed context is audit only, at its
exact path, marked "Value matched; context not confirmed". It never promotes a
verification rate, claim status or grade. A low-precision coincidence is at most
this value-only result. An ordinary context match also does not validate the
whole interpretation or enter the factual-claim counts.

The value index includes all numeric registry metrics, retained filing,
transcript and news text, retained analyst research/cases, and source-bound
report claims regardless of validation state. The filing quotation sentence
reader is shared. Analyst text is handed to deterministic verification outside
the model payload. Fresh runs include current attempts; resumed runs can also
use the same job's exact frozen-payload cohort, including failed writers'
retained research and rejected/partial cases. No cross-job or incompatible earlier payload is admitted.
Producer-bound SMA, 52-week endpoint, below-high and price/tangible-book
readings fix repeated context refusals. Explanatory parentheses and an explicit
shared money scale can establish only a value reading; explicit signs,
currencies, dimensions, periods and definition-changing modifiers stay guarded.

Original prose is retained. Live, Markdown and print show only recorded visible
notes; audit exports retain every result and original path. A single reader
sentence says unflagged figures are not necessarily verified. Assembly-owned
displays keep their contracts. Saved reports acquire no flags from display
alone. The judge prompt requires payload-grounded figures. There is no model
repair, new retrieval, larger model prompt or paid call.

Typed metrics can support execution only when a measured period reaches an
established office tenure by the report cutoff. An as-of date cannot replace
the measurement period. Dated decisions retain their existing tenure/source
checks. The legacy tenure number remains parseable but is omitted from the
judge request and reader surfaces; new values are derived only from an exact
established start and cutoff. Filing-backed office start wording remains
visible, including on saved unassessed cards.

ROIC, ROE, ROA, ROTE/ROTCE, WACC, CAGR, EBIT/EBITDA, NOPAT and ERP expansions use the same metric tokens
on source and prose. Different return definitions do not match. Data-only
synthesis counts classified data gaps; the old saved suffix is corrected only
when its exact deterministic wording and raw manifest count identify it.

Integration must advance the report-spec and Stage C pipeline stamps for the
new verification/schema/request behavior. The payload contents and registry
production are unchanged, so this change alone requires no payload stamp.
Version constants are deliberately left to integration. No Stage B valuation,
lease, currency or share-count implementation is changed. Stored reports and
evidence databases are immutable.

Offline replay visibly flags 58/59 original mutated figures: 6 contradictions
and 52 values not found. A catch requires the exact changed figure in the note
at its exact field path, including 307 to 407 days. The sole audit-only miss is
NVO disagreements[4].bullView: mutated sales-growth outlook 100% matches retained
1.0 completeness fractions, but no outlook context is confirmed. The mutation
set is unchanged. Rounding those same 59 mutations to integer precision in
their printed units gives 54/59 visible catches (6 contradictions, 48 not found;
5 audit only). Same-dimension, same-currency different-metric registry swaps on
those 59 paths give only 6/59 visible catches, all contradictions; 53 remain
audit only. This weak contextual detection rate is a limitation, not a verified
fact claim or a reason to relabel value matches as confirmations.

Unmodified visible fields: META 1, TSM 1, ASML 0, JPM 0, NVO 0. Both remaining
notes were read: META's USD 250 million-depositary-share offering converts a
share count to money; TSM's 30.0% year-one growth input is absent from retained
evidence in the current replay. Both are appropriate catches; zero false
alarms among these two visible fields. The latter can reflect historical model
drift; replay is not a factual-error rate for the original saved report. The
separate implementation report retains every note, mutation result and review.
All ten execution grades remain unchanged; NVO's CEO retains C on the
post-appointment June 2026 cash-flow evidence.

## D-200 - Filed figures over vendor conflicts (2026-11-04)

Revised by D-262: sibling flow admission requires the same statement quantity, not a component or combined-income proxy.

Implements source-data findings 1-5 and 8 from fair-value coverage baseline
`7ffa9fde`, on branch `t3/verify-data-fix`, implementation `0c9d8a9d`.
The remote branch was fetched and
merged with `--ff-only` before implementation. No parallel engineer's reserved
source area was edited. The earnings policy below is the final ordered rule.

### Earnings admission and provenance

1. For an exact issuer, period, currency and compatible filing set, adopt the
   **complete reconciled filed pretax, tax and net-income family** on a stated
   parent or consolidated basis, regardless of discrepancy size or sign. Keep
   the original vendor values in `fieldConflicts`, marked `usable: true` and
   `resolution: "filed-family"`, with filed provenance on each adopted field.
   Repeated later comparatives cannot conceal a complete original filing:
   resolve the original same-filing candidate before concluding there is no
   dispute or declaring the family incomplete. A genuinely SEC-sourced
   restatement retains its own compatible field provenance.
2. If that complete family cannot be recovered, keep the vendor family only
   when every exact-period conflict is same-sign and at most **1% of the larger
   absolute observation** (denominator floored at one currency unit). Notes
   give both observations; `resolution: "minor-retained"` distinguishes this
   allowance from filed verification. Do not attach filed provenance to the
   retained vendor amount.
3. Only an incomplete or unreconciled family with a discrepancy above 1%, or a
   sign conflict, is withheld. Name the conflicting field, both values and the
   incomplete-family reason. Refuse aliases and dependent earnings margins so
   later completion cannot restore the contradicted family.

Ownership alternatives and independently filed equity-method bridges remain
valid. A filed pretax line excluding equity-method income is bridged only with
the separately filed compatible equity-method amount. (Revised by D-237: the
bridged figure stays the pre-tax income of the earnings identity, and an
effective tax rate divides by the filed line itself, which the admission now
records beside it.) A separately filed
nonzero discontinued result prevents a continuing pretax/tax family from being
called a complete total-profit family. Consolidated, parent and common profit
are not interchangeable labels. Adoption reconciles their aliases and ratios;
continuing/discontinued aliases may be inferred only from the complete filed
continuing-pretax/tax-to-total-profit identity, with calculation provenance.

Dependent provider operating/nonoperating, cost, EBIT and EBITDA aggregates
that no longer reconcile use compatible filed operands or are qualified
individually, following the revenue admission rule. No balancing plug is
invented. Direct filed EPS can be adopted only when an already admitted raw
share count proves the same unchanged share unit and filing interval. No EPS
is inferred from profit; ADR conversions, split-adjusted counts and unresolved
million scaling cannot pass that direct ordinary-share check.

AIG Q3 2026 now admits **1,119M pretax - 270M tax = 849M consolidated profit**, with
**844M to common** and 5M noncontrolling profit. The immutable calculation view
and source-fact summary expose those available operands, with zero arithmetic
residual. Vendor -2,251M / -540M / -1,711M remains in the audit trail.
CAT FY2025 uses 11,541M pretax excluding equity-method profit plus 109M =
11,650M total pretax; less 2,768M tax gives 8,882M consolidated profit (8,884M
to common, NCI -2M). Its direct diluted EPS is 18.81, with 472.3M filed diluted
shares. USB uses 9,517M - 1,921M = 7,596M consolidated profit, preserving
7,570M parent and 7,194M common observations. ORCL FY2026 uses the reconciled
parent family 19,554M - 2,467M = 17,087M, with 16,984M to common.

### Accepted share, foreign EPS, revenue and cash rules

- Shares: compare after establishing the filed interval, including off-calendar
  fiscal years. The independent latest-count census has 76 numeric pairs, 50
  exact matches, rounding differences 0.0034% and 0.0088%, then 0.0170%.
  Permit at most 0.01% (at least one share), separately from the existing 3%
  unit/split test. Matching a different YTD duration is a period mismatch even
  inside that band. INTC FY2025 becomes 4,530M instead of 4,856M; BAC Q3 2026
  becomes 7,222.2M instead of the nine-month 7,312.5M. Existing corroborated
  scale repair and split-history protections remain.
- Foreign EPS: compare exact-period native currency using only the established
  ADS ratio, with conversion provenance and no FX dependency. SAP FY2025 uses
  6.10 EUR instead of 6.24. Frozen TSM facts stop at FY2024, so FY2025 is
  qualified; the saved primary filing's 65.47 TWD per ordinary share implies
  327.35 per ADS at five ordinary shares. No ratio is guessed for TM, SONY or
  BABA. NVO FY2025 23.03 DKK and ASML 24.71 EUR remain unchanged.

- Cash: repeated newer balances cannot suppress the original same-filing
  vendor comparison. SEC-sourced cash uses its own compatible field-level

All three review findings are **confirmed and fixed**:

1. **Original earnings recovery was skipped.** Exact-period later comparative
   provenance failed the vendor row's original filing-date gate for every
   operand, leaving an empty dispute list. Candidate resolution now runs before
   that conclusion: recover the original filing as a unit when the latest
   candidate is incompatible or incomplete, then detect conflicts. A synthetic
   original 1,000 / 200 / 800 family repeated by a later filing reproduced a
   surviving vendor -1,000 / -200 / -800 family before the fix. It now adopts
   the original filed profit with its original accession. A separate genuine
   SEC-built earnings restatement keeps its own compatible field provenance
   and is not reverted to the row's first-reporter date.
2. **SEC-built cash restatements were refused.** The statement builder's row
   `filingDate` identifies the first reporter, while cash's own provenance can
   identify a later restatement. Cash admission now selects exact accession,
   form and filing date from compatible cash-field provenance. Unproved vendor
   observations continue to compare with their original filing. A real
   SEC-builder synthetic control (100 original cash, 120 restated) failed first
   with cash, cash plus short-term investments and net debt all null; both
   enrichment and replay now retain 120 / 140 / 80. This uses actual builder
   output, not a manually labelled vendor row.
3. **Direct EPS was conditional on an outstanding monetary dispute.** The
   direct filed EPS check now runs independently when the complete monetary
   family already reconciles and share-unit proof is present. It still requires
   a raw same-unit count tie-out and compatible interval/filing; no EPS is
   derived from income and prior EPS/share refusals are respected. The test
   runs income-first acquisition and shares-first replay on the same immutable
   source: filed 1,000 / 200 / 800, diluted shares 100, EPS 8; vendor shares 102
   and EPS 8.02. Both orders now finish at 100 shares and EPS 8, with equal EPS
   provenance and vendor audit observations. Before the fix, fresh remained 8.02.
